articleTitle: Empirical Path Loss Channel Modeling at 28 GHz for Integrated Sensing and Communication System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) is considered as a potential technology of sixth-generation (6G). The ISAC system allows for communication and sensing through an integrated waveform, where the receiving strength of the signal affects system performance, including communication quality and sensing accuracy. The path loss characteristics directly affect the signal receiving strength. Most of the existing literature on ISAC path loss is based on the free space radar path loss, however, it does not contain the affect of near and far fields and scatterers in the environment. To address this issue, we conduct a channel measurement campaign at 28 GHz to analyze the path loss. Firstly, we find that path loss exhibits differences in the near and far fields: due to the near-field effect of sensing target, path loss exponent (PLE) fluctuates in the near-field while tends to stabilize in the far-field. Then based on the close-in (CI) reference distance model and the floating-intercept (FI) model, we obtain two empirical path loss models by separating the target influence for ISAC scenarios. Finally, we present detailed steps for path loss characteristic modeling, which can be used for ISAC channel simulation in future research.

articleTitle: Performance Optimization of UAV-Assisted Networks with mmWave Antennas
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV)-assisted network is emerging as a new promising solution to provide rapid deployment, high flexibility, and low-cost services for supporting civil and military applications. To ensure its stability and reliability under complex environmental conditions, we optimized the deployment of UAVs and antenna configuration, where the Matérn hard core point process (MHCPP) is used for UAV deployment and each UAV is equipped with millimeter wave (mmWave) antenna that can adjust beam width and radiation direction to enhance specific directional signal strength. Thus, we derived an approximate expression for the coverage probability under MHCPP distribution. Simulation results show that the network achievable throughput can be increased by up to 47%, and the coverage probability of typical GU reaching to an upper bound about 89%, which are illustrated significant advantages in performance improvement.

articleTitle: Path Metric Range Based Iterative Construction Method for Polar Codes
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In this paper, we consider the construction of polar codes for the successive cancellation list (SCL) decoding and propose a path metric range (PMR) based iterative construction method. In order to find the construction sequence for the SCL decoding, we simulate and calculate the PMRs and log-likelihood ratios (LLRs) of sub-channels to select the frozen bits and information bits, which is different from the the construction based on the successive cancellation (SC) decoding to calculate the error probability of sub-channels. The proposed construction can achieve 0.3 dB and 1.2 dB gain over the union-Bhattacharyya bound weight (SUBW) method and the Gaussian approximation (GA) method/polarization weight (PW) method in the SCL decoding algorithm, respectively. When using the CRC-aided SCL (CA-SCL) decoding, the proposed construction can also achieve 0.5 dB gain compared to traditional construction schemes.

articleTitle: Down-Link Slot Assignment in Beam Hopping Communication System Based on Genetic
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In recent years, satellite communication networks have attracted much attention due to their wide coverage. With the breakthrough of phased array antenna technology and the development of satellite Internet, which have diversified traffic types, space-time variation of traffic distribution and uneven traffic demand, multi-beam and beam-hopping technology has become an increasingly necessary part of satellite communication. In order to improve the resource utilization efficiency and communication quality of the highly dynamic LEO satellite system, a slot allocation method for hopping beam communication system based on genetic algorithm is studied, which responds to the current problems faced by satellite Internet. Genetic algorithm is a parallel, adaptive search solution space meta-heuristic algorithm, which can efficiently obtain the global optimal solution for sequence optimization problems. The simulation results show that our method can effectively reduce system interference, meet user requirements and achieve higher communication quality.

articleTitle: Nonbinary Zipper Codes Based on Reed-Solomon Codes
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In this paper, we study nonbinary zipper codes constructed based on Reed-Solomon (RS) codes. In addition, the sliding window decoding (SWD) based on adaptive belief propagation (ABP) is proposed. Furthermore, we propose the miscorrection mitigation algorithm by introducing a scaling factor β. Simulation results show that a rate 0.73 zipper code constructed by (63,55) RS code, using SWD based on ABP, has better performance than the SWD based on hard-decision decoding by 2.2 dB at a frame error rate (FER) of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−6</sup>.

articleTitle: RIS-Enhanced Wireless Powered MEC Networks: A Stackelberg Game-Based Energy Trading Framework
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: A reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) enhanced wireless powered mobile edge computing (MEC) network is considered, where an energy station (ES) first provides wireless charging to a passive Internet of Things device (IoTD), and then the IoTD leverages the collected energy for local computing and task offloading. We introduce an RIS to boost power transfer and task offloading efficiency by customizing an intelligent and controllable radio environment. A partial offloading (PO) scheme is proposed, where an energy trading framework is created based on Stackelberg game under the condition that the IoTD and ES are owned by two respective service suppliers. Specifically, the IoTD is required to provide payments to trade ES’s charging service, where the IoTD serves as a leader to maximize the difference between total computing bits’ revenues and charging payments, while the ES serves as a follower to maximize the difference between charging payments and charging costs. Through backward induction, the follower-level decision problem is first solved, and then the leader-level decision problem is processed via a block coordinate descent algorithm. Simulation results show that the proposed PO scheme obtains higher IoTD’s utilities than the full task offloading and full local computing schemes.

articleTitle: Average Peak Age of Information Minimization in UAV-assisted Integrated Sensing and Communication System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) is a promising technique to improve network communication and sensing capability by enhancing network coverage. In this paper, we consider a UAV-assisted ISAC system, where the UAV senses the target first and then transmitting the information sensing packet to base station (BS) for making decisions. Particularly, we adopt the peak age of information (PAoI) as a crucial performance metric to measure the freshness of the information. Our goal is to minimize the average PAoI by optimizing the horizontal position, sensing time, communication time, and power allocation of the UAV. For the single-target scenario, a semi-closed-form expression is obtained for the optimal horizontal location of the UAV, which is solved by Newton’s iterative method. For the multi-target scenario, we propose a successive convex approximation (SCA) method based algorithm to solve the non-convex problem. Finally, simulation results reveal the impact of various parameters and validate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithms.

articleTitle: Integrated Sensing and Communication Transmit Beamforming Design for Double-Function Receivers
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: This paper focuses on the beamforming design of a downlink integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system considering multiple passive eavesdropping targets. In the considered model, we use sensing signals as artificial noise to conceal confidential information for secure transmission. For efficient signal processing, beamforming schemes are proposed for both conventional and ISAC-dedicated receivers. We aim to minimize the overall transmission rate of all eavesdroppers for conventional receivers that cannot perform noise cancellation. To solve this problem, an iterative algorithm based on successive convex approximations is proposed. As for ISAC-dedicated receivers that can cancel interference, we propose a low-complexity iterative algorithm. Simulation results verify the superiority of the proposed algorithms.

articleTitle: Dispersion Curve Extraction and Source Localization for Single Hydrophone by Combining Image Skeleton Extraction with Advanced Time-Frequency Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Time-frequency analysis (TFA) transforms a one-dimensional signal into a two-dimensional image for its TF characteristics, which provides a framework that can be combined with digital image processing. In shallow water, a wide-band acoustic signal received by a hydrophone shows a unique dispersion structure, from which the source and propagation environment information can be obtained. This paper proposes a method combining two-subiteration skeleton extraction algorithm with advanced time-frequency analysis to separate and extract the dispersion curves from data received by a single hydrophone without any prior environmental information. The source location is then determined according to the time difference of dispersion curves.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence Based Feature Selection and Prediction of Downlink IP Throughput
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: With the rapid development of artificial intelligence, random forest is widely used in feature selection in wireless communication systems. Due to its ability to efficiently handle large data sets with high dimensions, random forest has become a popular machine learning method. The Downlink IP Throughput is a key indicator reflecting the real business experience of users in wireless communication systems. It is defined as the ratio of the amount of data sent downlink at the RLC layer to the data transmission time. This paper proposes a feature selection method based on random forest to predict Downlink IP Throughput. Before the random forest is used, the feature dimension is reduced in advance by calculating the variance of the features and filtering the features with low variance. Then, the random forest model is used to select the features that are highly sensitive to the Downlink IP Throughput and can mostly affect and reflect the change of the Downlink IP Throughput, and the feature set that affects the Downlink IP Throughput is constructed, and the MLP model is built to predict the Downlink IP Throughput. The model uses real data such as user scheduling information and user throughput measurement information to train and test the prediction model. The experimental results show that the model successfully selects the key features that affect the Downlink IP Throughput, and shows good performance in the Downlink IP Throughput prediction.

articleTitle: Dynamic Power Allocation in NOMA-Based Federated Learning System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: With the rapid rise of digital technology, artificial intelligence driven by big data has entered the fast lane of development, but it has also given rise to many problems, such as data silos and user privacy. A solution to solve these problems is federated learning. However, this framework also faces many challenges, with high communication costs in the first place. Non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) can be applied to alleviate the problem. In this paper, we focus on this issue and investigate multiple access technology based on federated learning. We build a NOMA-based federated learning system to improve the communication efficiency of federated learning. Then we propose a NOMA dynamic power allocation algorithm based on the realtime channel state at the edge user to improve the performance of the system. Experimental results show that the proposed algorithm can improve the training accuracy of the system model and reduce the energy consumption for uploading parameters.

articleTitle: Product-Matrix Construction of Minimum Storage Rack-aware Regenerating Codes
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In data centers, storage nodes are typically organized in racks and the cross-rack communication cost is often much higher than the intra-rack communication cost. Minimum Storage Rack-aware Regenerating (MSRR) codes are special maximum distance separable (MDS) array codes that can achieve the minimum cross-rack repair bandwidth for single node failures. In this paper, we present an explicit construction of MSRR codes by employing the product-matrix framework. Our product-matrix MSRR codes have lower sub-packetization level than the existing MSRR codes.

articleTitle: Identity-aware Pseudo-Supervision Face Image Super-resolution for Surveillance Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Generic super-resolution models adopt a predefined degradation kernel (e.g., Gaussian) or estimate the degradation kernel from low-resolution images to downsample high-resolution images as the training data, because there are few low-resolution and high-resolution image pairs. However, the low-resolution images captured in surveillance scenarios are severely impacted by capture distance, illumination, occlusion, etc., so the degradation kernel is too complicated to predefine or estimate. Meanwhile, identity preservation is significant for face image super-resolution. To this end, we propose identity-aware pseudo-supervision face image super-resolution in real-world scenarios, especially surveillance scenarios. We utilize Generative Adversarial Nets (GAN) to degenerate high-resolution images to follow the distribution of low-resolution images captured by surveillance cameras. The synthesized low-resolution images and corresponding high-resolution compose paired training data with pseudo-supervision. Furthermore, to preserve the identity during the degeneration, a face image quality assessment module is plugged into the degeneration module, which balances the degradation and identity preservation. We conduct extensive experiments on multiple benchmarks to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A MSE-Based Interference Exploitation 1-Bit Precoding for QAM Constellations
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Compared to high-resolution digital-to-analog converters (DACs), deploying 1-bit DACs require much less hardware complexity and power consumption of a massive multi-user multi-input multi-output (MU-MIMO) system. However, when only 1-bit DACs are used, it is more challenging to mitigate or exploit multi-user interference (MUI) because the feasible domain of a transmit signal is non-smooth. Particularly, when non-constant envelope constellations such as quadrature amplitude modulation (QAM) constellations are used, it is impractical to perfectly eliminate the destructive interference. In this paper, we investigate symbol-level MUI exploiting methods for massive MU-MIMO systems under 1-bit DACs. Because MUIs can be constructive or destructive, we define a modified mean square error (MSE) metric for QAM constellations to evaluate the effect of both MUIs and noise. Then, the 1-bit constrained sum modified MSE minimization precoding problem is modeled as a piecewise-defined mixed integer linear programming problem, where transmit vector and receiving processing factors for all users are optimization variables. To solve that problem, we design an efficient algorithm by iteratively updating receiving processing factors and the transmit vector. Numerical results show that our proposed precoding method could effectively improve the symbol decision performance.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of a Non-terrestrial Network with Timing Advance Compensation in 3GPP
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Non-terrestrial network (NTN) have been recognized as a key technology for providing large-scale connectivity and wide coverage in 5th-generation (5G) networking. Nevertheless, they face many challenges, such as high delay and service continuity. For a non-geostationary Earth orbit satellite, the high orbital speed of the satellite means that the timing advance (TA) will change more rapidly than in a terrestrial network, thereby necessitating frequent closed-loop TA updates from the network, such as timing advance commands (TACs). However, it may not be up-to-date when they arrive at the user equipment (UE) because of the large propagation delay, it will also consume more transmission resources. Nevertheless, the TA variation due to satellite movement is quite predictable, and this can be configured into the UE as a timing drift (TD) to minimize the update frequency of TACs from the network. In this contribution, we propose a beam-specific timing drift rate (TDR) scheme. We also demonstrate, through simulation results, the impact of configuring a TDR value into the UE that can be used for updating closed-loop and open-loop TAs without the need for frequent TACs, additional, the proposed solution is evaluated to reduce the ISI ratio and obtain throughput gain.

articleTitle: CNN-Conformer: Conformer in Channel Mapping Based Convolutional Neural Network for Stereophonic Acoustic Echo Cancellation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In acoustic echo cancellation (AEC), conventional methods estimate the path of the microphone and loudspeaker to achieve clear communication. However, for stereophonic AEC (SAEC), the problem of non-uniqueness arises because of a high correlation between far-end signals. This paper proposes a convolutional neural network (CNN) with a conformer module to remove echoes and background noise. First, the generalized cross-correlation (GCC) is utilized to align the far-end signals with the echoes in the microphone signal. After that, the complex spectral features are fed into the CNN-Conformer, where the encoder module is used to extract the frequency information, the conformer module explores the channel relationship, and the temporal convolutional network (TCN) module performs time modeling. Finally, a joint loss function in the time domain and frequency domain is designed to train the network. The experiments show that the proposed approach presents a good generalization capability and performs better than previous neural network-based approaches in SAEC.

articleTitle: Control Delay and Load Based Controller Placement in LEO Satellite Network
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: The Software-Defined Network (SDN) architecture offers flexible management for Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite network, enhancing scalability and efficiency in the integrated satellite-terrestrial network. However, the dynamic topology induces constant changes in communication links between satellites, and the uneven distribution of ground traffic results in varying flow requests. Consequently, dynamic adjustments in controller placement become essential to accommodate these network changes. In this paper, a control delay and load based controller placement (DLCP) mechanism is proposed to address this issue. DLCP assesses the impact of flow requests on control delay, formulates the initial and dynamic controller placement problems (CPP) to reduce the control delay and flow setup time, and subsequently solves them using an improved heuristic algorithm. Simulation results demonstrate that the dynamic controller placement adjustment of DLCP yields superior performance in terms of average flow setup time and packet drop rate.

articleTitle: Construction of generalized Čech complex for coverage hole detection in 3-dimensional space
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Homology theory has been introduced to address the coverage hole detection problem in the networks covering 2-dimensional regions, whereas the coverage of 3-dimensional space has received limited attention. In this paper, a construction method of generalized Čech complex is proposed for coverage hole detection in 3-dimensional space. The simplices whose dimension are equal or lower than three are built successively to obtain the complex, and then the homology groups of the complex are calculated to see the existence of coverage holes. In particular, the construction criteria of 3-simplices is presented detailedly, which include selection of candidate groups and check of four different situations. The effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is verified on various cases, and the simulation results confirm an accurate detection of coverage holes. Additionally, the complexity of the algorithm is estimated to be in polynomial time, indicating its computational efficiency.

articleTitle: Intelligent Multi-peak Beam Training in mmWave Communications with Deep Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In the mmWave communication network, exhaustive beam search (EBS) assisted beam training is suggested for accurate beam alignment between the access point (AP) and the user equipment (UE) in the existing 3GPP standard. Nevertheless, the EBS method suffers from unacceptable training overheads, which may degrade the network throughput, especially when the beam space is large. In this paper, we propose an intelligent multi-peak beam training algorithm to tackle this issue. The main idea of the algorithm lies in, by applying binary encoding into the narrow beam index, several multi-peak wide beams can be constructed. Then, a deep neural network (DNN) is carefully designed and trained to decode the probed signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs) of multi-peak wide beams into the optimal narrow beam index. With the well-trained DNN, the optimal narrow beam can be identified online by feeding the probed SNRs of the multi-peak wide beams into the DNN. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm outperforms the state of the arts in terms of overheads and throughput.

articleTitle: Secrecy Outage Analysis of RIS-Assisted Multiuser Scheduling in Underlay Cognitive Radio Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: This paper investigates the secrecy performance of a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) assisted underlay cognitive radio network consisting of multiple cognitive transmitters (CTs) communicating to a common cognitive receiver (CR) with the assistance of a RIS, while an eavesdropper (E) attempts to tap the confidential information transmissions from the CTs via RIS to CR. To secure the RIS-assisted CT-CR communications, we propose the following multiuser scheduling schemes, namely, the RIS-assisted round-robin multiuser scheduling (RRMS), the RIS-assisted opportunistic multiuser scheduling with full channel state information (ROMS-FCSI), and the RIS-assisted opportunistic multiuser scheduling with partial channel state information (ROMS-PCSI). Specifically, the ROMS-FCSI is designed depending on the availability of channel state information (CSI) of the legitimate transmission links from the CTs via RIS to CR, the interference links from the CTs via RIS to PR, and the eavesdropping links from the CTs via RIS to E. By contrast, the ROMS-PCSI only requires the CSI of legitimate transmission links without knowing the CSI of eavesdropping and interference links. We derive closed-form secrecy outage probability (SOP) expressions of the RRMS, ROMS-FCSI, and ROMS-PCSI schemes over Rayleigh fading channels. Additionally, the correctness of our derived SOP expressions is validated by extensive Monte-Carlo simulation results. Also, numerical results show that the ROMS-FCSI scheme achieves the best secrecy performance and the RRMS scheme performs the worst in terms of the SOP. Moreover, as the number of RIS reflecting elements increases, the SOP performance of the RRMS, ROMS-FCSI, and ROMSPCSI schemes improves accordingly.

articleTitle: Offloading Model of 5G Intelligent Terminal Based on UC-MEC and Node Consensus Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Offloading for 5G intelligent terminals is an important requirement of mobile edge computing (MEC), which can reduce the load of terminal devices and provide more powerful computing power and services. However, due to the interference between different users and the waste of a lot of resources, the role of MEC is greatly limited. In the article, energy-saving blockchain technology is introduced into the user-centric MEC (UC-MEC) system. However, in UC-MEC, it is necessary to comprehensively consider task offloading and energy consumption optimization in the consensus process to improve overall energy efficiency. To solve these problems, a new offloading model of 5G intelligent terminal is proposed, which realizes safe and efficient resource utilization by jointly optimizing the bandwidth and computing resource allocation of access point (AP). The research also proposed a resource consensus mechanism based on Zookeeper atomic broadcast (RC-ZAB), and the parallel optimization framework of relaxed hybrid alternative direction method of multipliers (RH-ADMM) to solve the problems of resource transaction and energy consumption optimization. The experimental results show that compared with the comparison method, the total energy consumption of the proposed method is reduced by 41.39% at most, and the total delay is reduced by 29.80% at most.

articleTitle: A Regularized Neural Optimization Approach with Beta Densities for Blind Deconvolution
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In the field of image blind deblurring, existing deep learning deblurring networks can learn from a large number of paired training images, but are limited in dealing with a variety of complex large-size blur kernels. The underlying reason is that, those networks are not sufficiently generalized to unseen blurs, and hence, it is necessary to explore a proper regularizer so as to better constrain the problem. In this paper, we are inspired by the Beta probability density function, and empirically find that it has a great potential in discriminating between the blurred images and sharp images. With such an observation, we try to investigate the prior under the maximum-a-posterior framework so as to benefit the deep learning methods. In specific, this paper proposes a regularized neural optimization approach with beta densities for blind deblurring. In difference to most existing deep learning methods, the proposed approach has greatly benefited from the model-based scheme in terms of both hand-crafted and self-learned priors. With amounts of experiments on synthetic datasets as well as real datasets, and we find that the recovered images show good performance, the proposed method is shown comparative or better performance than state-of-art algorithms.

articleTitle: Outage Performance of C-NOMA-Assisted Cognitive Satellite-Terrestrial Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: This paper introduces cooperative non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) into a cognitive satellite-terrestrial network to improve the system performance. Specifically, both the secondary transmitter (ST) and the full-duplex (FD) secondary receiver (SR) are proposed to cooperate with the primary user (PU). The ST can transmit superposed signal of primary message from the satellite and the secondary message to the PU and SR simultaneously by NOMA protocol, while the SR also cooperates with the PU to forward the primary message based on the FD protocol. Closed-form approximate expressions for the outage probabilities of the PU and SR are derived. Then, the diversity order of the PU is also obtained. It is shown that the diversity order of the PU can be improved by 1 compared to the existing work that the SR does not cooperate. Monte Carlo simulations confirm the correctness of the theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: An Enhanced Artificial Immune Based Base Station Planning Approach for Wireless Networks with Uneven User Distribution
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Base station (BS) planning has always been a challenging task, especially in ultra-dense heterogeneous Networks (HetNets) with miniatured and densely deployed BSs. In this paper, we propose an enhanced artificial immune based BS planning approach for two-layer HetNets with uneven user distribution. The goal is to minimize the deployment costs while ensuring coverage and capacity. BS locations is optimized and redundant BSs are eliminated. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme performs well in terms of convergence and finding the optimal solution.

articleTitle: A Meta-Learning based Gradient Descent Algorithm for MU-MIMO Beamforming
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Multi-user multiple-input multiple-output (MU-MIMO) beamforming design is typically formulated as a non-convex weighted sum rate (WSR) maximization problem that is known to be NP-hard. This problem is solved either by iterative algorithms, which suffer from slow convergence, or more recently by using deep learning tools, which require time-consuming pre-training process. In this paper, we propose a low-complexity meta-learning based gradient descent algorithm. A meta network with lightweight architecture is applied to learn an adaptive gradient descent update rule to directly optimize the beamformer. This lightweight network is trained during the iterative optimization process, which we refer to as training while solving, which removes both the training process and the data-dependency of existing deep learning based solutions. Extensive simulations show that the proposed method achieves superior WSR performance compared to existing learning-based approaches as well as the conventional weighted minimum mean square error (WMMSE) algorithm, while enjoying much lower computational load.

articleTitle: A Fast Algorithm for Finding the Roots of Polynomials over Finite Fields
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Finding all roots of polynomials over finite fields is a crucial problem in algebraic coding techniques, such as decoding BCH codes and Reed-Solomon codes. The current commonly used methods are Chien search or fast Fourier transform (FFT), which evaluates all elements in a finite field and results in field multiplications whose number increases linearly with the field size. In this paper, we propose a new approach that enables the multiplicative complexity to grow sub-linearly with the field size. To our knowledge, this is the currently lowest multiplicative complexity for this problem. Additionally, the proposed approach maintains the additive complexity similar to that of FFT-based method.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Successive Cancellation Priority Decoder with Iteratively-increased Searching Width for Polar Codes
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: The successive cancellation list (SCL) decoding of polar codes can achieve a performance close to the maximum-likelihood (ML) decoding while large list size results in high computational complexity. To this end, successive cancellation priority (SCP) decoding is proposed to reduce the complexity of the SCL decoding with acceptable space complexity. In this paper, an adaptive SCP (ADSCP) decoder with iteratively increased searching width is proposed. Two priority queues are applied to store all the priority nodes during the decoding. When the correct decoding path cannot be obtained with the current searching width, the decoding continues with a larger searching width rather than be restarted. Furthermore, an early termination criterion is applied to quit the decoding when too many inefficient path extensions are performed based on a preset threshold. The early termination criterion can reduce the worst-case complexity of the decoder. Simulation results show that given the same searching width (list size), the proposed ADSCP decoder can achieve the same decoding performance as the conventional adaptive SCL (ADSCL) decoder while significantly reducing the complexity.

articleTitle: OTFS Channel Estimation With Superimposed Pilots Based on Compressed Sensing
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) modulation has shown better performance in high-mobility communication scenarios compared to orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) systems in recent years. Conventional OTFS channel estimation scheme requires guard symbols around pilot symbols to prevent pilot-data interference, which results in a loss of spectral efficiency and high peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR). Hence, in this paper, we propose a partially superimposed pilot scheme, where data symbols are distributed in all the delay-Doppler (DD) bins and pilot symbols are superimposed on them partially. In our scheme, we only need part of the OTFS frame for channel estimation rather than the entire frame in existing superimposed pilot scheme, which reduces complexity significantly. We utilize the sparsity of the DD channel, establish the compressed sensing (CS) model through the double block-cyclic characteristics of sensing matrix and transform the channel estimation problem into a sparse signal recovery problem. We also propose an iterative algorithm to alleviate the pilot interference at the receiver. Moreover, we obtain the optimum pilot-to-data ratio (PDR) through simulations. Simulation results show that the proposed scheme achieves better performance compared to the existing superimposed pilot scheme.

articleTitle: Age of Information in Uplink Cellular-Connected UAV Networks with Nakagami-m Fading Channels
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are increasingly employed in various sensing applications, highlighting the need for efficient communication systems. Age of Information (AoI) is a critical metric to assess the timeliness of information in wireless networks. As a promising architecture, cellular-connected UAV network has been widely discussed in both academia and industry. However, the AoI in uplink cellular-connected UAV networks has not been fully investigated. To bridge this gap, in this paper, we propose an analytical framework to evaluate the AoI performance of uplink cellular-connected UAV network by considering the practical Nakagami-m fading channels. By leveraging stochastic geometry, we first derive the negative integer b<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> moments of uplink conditional success probability of the typical UAV, which is further used to derive the analytical expressions for average AoI and the variance of AoI. The analytical results provide insight and trade-offs for optimizing AoI in the network under consideration.

articleTitle: Frequency Hopping Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) has circumvented OMA’s connectivity limitations, providing new possibilities to achieve a larger connection. One of the most popular uplink NOMA schemes is sparse code multiple access (SCMA). Massive research has been made on SCMA, which focuses on the codebook design and low complexity multi-user detector (MUD). We are interested in how to maximize the connectivity ability of code domain NOMA with tolerable complexity of the receiver. In this paper, a frequency hopping (FH)-based NOMA is proposed. Under this scheme, the spreading factor (SF) is reduced to one to accommodate a larger connection. The system adopts frequency hopping technique to increase the system diversity and promote extrinsic information interaction between users. A heuristic frequency hopping sequence allocation method is proposed , which succeeds in uniformly transmitting users’ signals on the resource block. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed scheme. And we notice that FH-NOMA is more adaptable to non-ideal channels. Experiments show that FH-NOMA has superior performance than SCMA under higher user load and higher spectral efficiency requirements.

articleTitle: Radar Signal Recognition Based on Deep Feature Fusion of Multiple Time-frequency Images
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Radar signal recognition is an important topic in electronic countermeasures, which faces great challenges in low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) scenarios. To address this issue, a new method for radar signal recognition based on deep feature fusion with multiple time-frequency images (TFIs) is proposed. Specifically, we first transform time-domain radar signals into TFIs, and then utilize a deep neural network to extract informative features for modulation recognition. To make full use of time-frequency features from various TFIs, we propose a multi-channel fusion model that merges the three TFIs of a radar signal obtained through the short-time Fourier transform (STFT), Choi-Williams distribution (CWD) transform and multi-synchronous squeezing transform (MSST) into a comprehensive TFI. An improved VGG-Net is employed to perform feature extraction from the combined images and modulation classification for radar signal recognition. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method can achieve an overall recognition accuracy of over 90% for twelve typical radar signals at an SNR of -6dB, indicating its effectiveness under low SNR conditions.

articleTitle: Safety Stock Forecasting based on Materials Correlation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Safety stock is an inventory to cope with the randomness and risk in all aspects of supply, production, and sales. In order to solve the problems of low inventory level leading to production interruption and high inventory level leading to high inventory cost and overstocking, safety inventory forecasting is needed. With the consideration, we propose a safety stock forecasting method based on spatial-temporal sequence model. Firstly, we adopt a clustering method based on time series shape to classify the materials, and the results of the classification are used as classification prior knowledge to enhance the prediction performance. Then, the dosage forecasting model is established for different classes, respectively. By proposing the correlation matrix, the co-occurrence frequency of different materials in the product dosage pattern is used as the adjacency matrix, which is correlation prior knowledge. With the combined effect of classification and correlation prior knowledge, the accuracy of predicting the dosage of a specific material can be greatly improved in a period of time in the future. Through experiments, it is proved that our method greatly improves the prediction accuracy and successfully explores the correlation between materials, compared with the traditional method.

articleTitle: Video Experience Optimization Solutions for 5G-Advanced and 6G Best Network
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: With the evolution of 5G-Advanced and 6G technology, video services proportion become higher, how to guarantee E2E video experience is a difficult problem. Firstly, the paper analyzes the typical video E2E delay model and proposes simple delay model and key optimization directions for better E2E video experience. Then, the paper analyzes the initial stage experience improvement solutions and proposes the concept of 3s theory, Finally the paper obtains the relationship of the initial stage delay and air interface throughput by the theoretical and practical network test results.

articleTitle: Improved Feedback-Enabled Fountain Codes for High-Efficiency Broadcasting
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: With the rapidly increasing growth of digital video services, higher demands are placed on the reliability of broadcast communications. In this paper, we investigate broadcast schemes of fountain codes with feedback. We first propose an improved scheme based on non-uniform selection, which utilizes feedback to exclude useless source symbols from the selection range. In order to enhance the effectiveness of coded symbols, we further improve the proposed scheme by introducing the concatenated structure with fixed-rate pre-coding. Simulation results demonstrate that proposed schemes attain higher spectral efficiency compared to existing broadcast schemes.

articleTitle: A Survey on the Application and Development of Commercial Communication Constellations in the U.S. Military Operations System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: The role of the "Star Link" in the Russian-Ukrainian war has attracted wide attention. The commercial communication constellation has become a space equipment force that cannot be underestimated for the US military. How does the US military integrate the commercial communication constellations into its operational system? What is the future development trend of the military application of commercial communication constellations? In this paper, we summarize the adjustment of the organization structure and the defense experiments for commercial communication constellations, then analyze the military application mode and development trend of commercial communication constellations. The analysis results will provide reference for the research of the US space operational system and the development of commercial communication constellations in China.

articleTitle: Computing Redundancy in Blocking Systems: Fast Service or No Service
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Redundancy in distributed computing systems reduces job completion time. It is widely employed in practice and studied in theory for queuing systems, often in a low-traffic regime where queues remain empty. Motivated by emerging edge systems, this paper initiates a study of using redundancy in blocking systems. Edge nodes often operate in highly unpredictable environments, and replicating job execution improves the job mean execution time. However, directing more resources to some computing jobs will block the execution of others. We evaluate the system performance using two metrics: job computing time and job blocking probability. We show that the job computing time decreases with increasing replication factor, but the job blocking probability does not. Therefore, there is a tradeoff. Interestingly, some minimal replication significantly reduces computing time with almost no blocking probability change. This paper proposes the system service rate as a new combined metric to evaluate the tradeoff and a single system’s performance indicator. We conclude that the optimal number replication factor that maximizes the system service rate changes with the distribution parameters and the arrival rate.

articleTitle: A Fast Estimation Method of the Augmented Cyclic Spectrum for Improper Signals
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: The cyclic spectrum (CS) is widely applied in various signal parameter estimation fields in communications and radar. Traditionally, these estimation methods only consider the CS. However, recent works have shown that for improper signals, there exists conjugate cyclic spectrum (CCS) as these signals have unique second-order (SO) statistic compared with proper signals. In this paper, we first derive the augmented cyclic spectrum (ACS) expression for improper signals and propose a fast estimation method to estimate the ACS based on FFT accumulation (FAM) algorithm. Our results show that, the ACS can provide an additional degree of freedom (DoF) for signal parameter estimation of improper signals. Besides, we select maximum improper signals as an example, and apply the widely linear frequency shifted (WL-FRESH) filter structure to suppress severe co-channel interference (CCI) by fully exploiting the augmented cyclic frequency of improper signals. Numerical results show that the proposed WL-FRESH can take advantage of the additional conjugate cyclic frequencies induced by the improper signals and thus obtain significant performance improvements.

articleTitle: Transmission Power Allocation of RIS-Aided Cell-Free mMIMO for Downlink URLLC Service
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Cell-free Massive MIMO is a potential technology direction of the beyond-5G network, which can achieve higher network capacity and energy efficiency. The distributed nature of reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) deployment has natural compatibility with cell-free networks, and RIS has the potential to reduce the cost of the network. This paper studies the downlink transmission power allocation in a RIS-Aided cell-free massive MIMO network for Ultra reliable and low-latency communication (URLLC). We propose a scheme that considers joint RIS optimization and downlink power allocation to optimize the sum URLLC achievable rate. Numerical results show that the sum URLLC achievable rate of RIS-Aided cell-free massive MIMO is enhanced further with the assistance of RIS and the optimization scheme proposed in this paper.

articleTitle: Fine-grained Lung Function Sensing based on Millimeter-Wave Radar
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has posed a significant threat to the health of elderly individuals, particularly those with respiratory conditions. Therefore, daily monitoring of lung capacity is necessary to assess the pulmonary condition and initiate timely treatment measures. This paper aims to explore an effective non-contact method for fine-grained pulmonary function sensing. Specifically, we propose to utilize millimeter-wave radar to contactless sensing of the overall chest and abdominal motion. Then the LUNet (Lung Unet) is constructed to recover the Expiratory Volume (EV) curves using the entire motion information of the chest and abdomen. Finally, the pulmonary function indicators are extracted based on the predicted EV curve directly. The experimental results demonstrate that the average correlation of the predicted EV curve is 96.74% and the mean relative errors for FEV1, FVC, and FEV1/FVC are 7.73%, 8.15%, and 6.70%, respectively. These results suggest that our method has the potential for clinical monitoring and assessment of respiratory diseases.

articleTitle: Slotted ALOHA-based URA Scheme with Index Modulation for Short Block Length
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Unsourced random access (URA) has become a promising technique to support massive connectivity scenarios. This work proposes a slotted ALOHA-based URA scheme with index modulation for short packet transmission under Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) channel. In our scheme, the short data packet of each active user is divided into three parts, where the first two parts are encoded by compressed sensing (CS) and the low-density-parity-check (LDPC) code, respectively, while the third part is the index of the slot where the encoded packet is transmitted. The data decoding is implemented slot-by-slot at the base station (BS). To this end, a hard decision (HD)-based decoder, including the index modulation demodulation, CS decoding, and LDPC decoding, is developed. Simulation results reveal that our proposal outperforms the counterparts significantly.

articleTitle: S2TGAN: A GAN-Based Mobile Video Streaming Generation Model for Stalling Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Due to the complex and dynamic nature of the wireless network environment, data-driven model often requires a significant amount and diversity of training data, leading to a challenging difficulty of stalling detection with high performance, especially at the client side. To address this issue, a novel Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) based data generation model Seq2Seq-TCN GAN (S2TGAN) is proposed in this paper for both chunk-based and stream-based video streaming sequences in order to further improve the performance of stalling detection of video on demand (VoD) and live video streaming (LVS). Resorting to Seq2Seq, the generator is constructed to generate video streaming sequences under the control of stalling information, and the discriminator adopts Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) to extract more discriminative temporal features of video streaming sequences. Meanwhile, Iman-Conover method is used to incorporate domain knowledge to guide the generation of video streaming and improve the fidelity of synthetic data. A LVS dataset collected from HuYa and DouYu is carefully prepared to verify the generation performance of proposed model, as well as a public RequetDataSet. Extensive experimental results indicate that the proposed model can outperform the other state-of-the-arts in terms of maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) and Train on synthetic, Test on Real (TSTR) evaluation methods of stalling detection.

articleTitle: Detection Probability of PRACH Employing Carrier Frequency Offset Compensation at UE Transmission in NR Uplink
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: This paper proposes physical random access channel (PRACH) transmission employing carrier frequency offset (CFO) compensation that is measured at a set of user equipment (UE) using the synchronization signal block (SSB) in the New Radio (NR) uplink. Computer simulation results show that by using cyclic prefix (CP) based fractional frequency offset (FFO) estimation and joint integer frequency offset (IFO) estimation with the primary synchronization signal, the correct FFO and IFO estimation probabilities of 90% are achieved at the average received signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of approximately -4 dB and -8 dB, respectively at a UE receiver. Accordingly, we show that when the average received SNR at the UE receiver is higher than approximately -5 dB, the miss-detection probability (MDP) of the proposed PRACH transmission with the CFO compensation at UE transmission is almost identical to that without CFO. We also show that the PRACH transmission with CFO compensation at UE transmission achieves almost the same PRACH MDP as that without CFO for the frequency stability of a UE local oscillator of up to 10 ppm when the average received SNR at the UE receiver is higher than approximately 0 dB.

articleTitle: Stochastic Geometry Analysis of Air-to-Ground Communication Networks With Circular Trajectory
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In this work, we utilize stochastic geometry to investigate the performance of mobile unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) networks providing ground coverage service in post-disaster scenarios or coverage blind areas. The location of ground users is modeled as a Poisson cluster process (PCP) to represent the distribution clustering of ground users in these scenarios, i.e., node clusters in internet of things (IoT). A flying UAV serving as aerial base station (ABS) is forced to move around a cluster center with circular trajectory to provide information coverage service for that user cluster. By considering the periodic fluctuation of network topology caused by the movement of UAVs, we derive the success probability (SP) with Type-I hybrid automatic repeat request (HARQ) retransmission scheme. The simulation results verify the correctness of theoretical results and demonstrate the effect of key parameters on transmission performance.

articleTitle: Waveform Design for Integrated Sensing and Communication Using Random Stepped-carrier OFDM Signals
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In this paper, a random stepped-carrier orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (RSC-OFDM) waveform is designed for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC), where the information is conveyed not only by M-ary signal constellations, but also by the steps index. In addition, a radar processing scheme is proposed to realize the high resolution range-velocity image, where the phase error induced by steps is compensated through the velocity estimation. The scheme is verified with simulations at 60 GHz. Simulation results show that the proposed scheme outperforms the conventional method by improving the range resolution, while keeping the nearly constant computational effort.

articleTitle: Flexible Resource Allocation Scheme for Non-Overlapping Subband Full Duplex Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: To pursue lower latency and higher uplink data rate in time division duplex (TDD) systems, full duplex is introduced in 5G networks. This paper first analyzes the frame structure of in-band full duplex and non-overlapping subband full duplex (SBFD). Then, the interference signals are studied. Especially, the interferences are modeled in the typical SBFD scenarios. Finally, the system level simulations of SBFD are conducted in nine cases considering different uplink and downlink subband bandwidth configuration in indoor scenarios. The simulation results demonstrate that, in large packet scenario, a tradeoff between uplink performance gain and downlink degradation should be made in SBFD, in small packer scenario, SBFD can enhance the uplink performance and reduce the latency remarkably with negligible downlink degradation by configuring appropriate uplink bandwidth.

articleTitle: Image Deblurring based on a U-shaped Network for Vehicle Surveillance Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Motion blur is a common problem in the field of surveillance scenarios, and obstructs the acquisition of valuable information. With the development of deep learning (DL) technologies, a series of CNN-based methods have been developed for image deblurring and achieved significant improvement. However, most existing deblurring methods aim to handle the global blur while in practical local blur is more common. For example, the motion blur is caused by local moving vehicles and the performances of the current methods are poor in the vehicle surveillance scenarios. Based on this observation, this paper proposes a deblurring method, called DeVeh, for the vehicle surveillance scenarios. The architecture of the proposed method is mainly based on a U-shaped network (UNet), and applies an Intersection over Patch (IoP) factor and a supervised morphological loss to improve the performance on the local blur. To verify the effectiveness, a moving vehicle dataset is established over real surveillance scenarios. Comparative and ablation experimental analysis are carried out over it. As a result, our proposal achieves better performance compared to the existing benchmarks.

articleTitle: A Hamming Code based Anti-Frequency Offset Mapping Scheme with LoRa Modulation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: To overcome large frequency offset without the extra pilot overhead, we propose a Hamming code based anti-frequency offset mapping scheme for LoRa modulation system, where a new mapping rule between the Hamming codewords and the modulation symbols is designed. Furthermore, a novel detection strategy is introduced based on the mapping scheme. Specifically, the received symbol is estimated by considering the values of two adjacent samples in frequency domain. Simulation results show that the Hamming coded LoRa system with the proposed mapping scheme performs much better than the traditional scheme in the presence of large frequency offset, and achieves a good tradeoff between the error performance and the ability of anti-frequency offset.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Simulation and Verification System for Mega-Constellation Satellite Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Satellite networks have the characteristics of heterogeneous nodes, high dynamics and multiple application scenarios, and they break through the inherent defects of traditional terrestrial network protocols in satellite network design. It is necessary to build a simulation and verification system for mega-constellation satellite networks, laying a foundation for satellite network systems to carry out on-orbit verification and typical application demonstrations. In this paper, a simulation and verification system for mega-constellation is designed. Specifically, the overall architecture of the system is defined, and the functional modules of the system and the performance indices supported are described. Finally, we study the elastic networking mechanism of mega-constellations under variable space-time scales, verify intelligent elastic network architecture and the routing protocol.

articleTitle: A Trusted Architecture Based on Semantic Communication for Matching Data and Models
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In this paper, a new layered architecture named Trusted Sub-layer (TSL) is proposed, which features a matching mechanism for protecting the privacy security of data and models effectively based on the different protection levels required. Specifically, TSL is designed to perform three processes to map adapted codec models for specific data transmission tasks, including the Confirmation of Data and Semantic Codec Models, the Trusted Matching (TM) and the Trusted Handshake Protocol for Semantic Transceivers. Moreover, the process of TM is experimentally simulated based on different TM algorithms. And the effects of the number and distribution of privacy features on matching error rate are analyzed. The results show that the Transformer-based TM algorithm achieves the privacy protection effects at 96.5% when the number of privacy features is 6. Finally, the applicability of the algorithm on general nodes of terminal devices is discussed.

articleTitle: Tree Search Based Symbol Detection for Multi-Band Petahertz Communication With Adjacent-Band Crosstalk
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: For Petahertz communication (PetaCom) employing multi-band transmission, the crosstalk mainly occurs between adjacent bands when a suitable optical filter is adopted at each detector. In this case, the channel matrix can be modeled as a tridiagonal matrix. Utilizing this fact, this work proposes a simplified tree search method for symbol detection in multi-band PetaCom, which does not require QL decomposition and can significantly reduce the computational complexity compared with conventional maximum-likelihood (ML) detection sphere decoding (SD). Experimental measurement verifies the model of tridiagonal channel matrix. Besides, simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method can achieve the same symbol error rate as ML detection and SD, while involving much less running time.

articleTitle: A Muti-beam Placement Optimization Scheme in LEO Beam Hopping Satellite Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Beam hopping (BH) technology has emerged as a solution for low earth orbit (LEO) satellite communication system to better utilize the limited resources onboard. This technology serves the region with fewer but flexible spot beams which dynamically point to users based on their location and traffic needs by taking advantage of phased array antenna. However, in some cases, some of the users are located at the edge of the beam and a large number of beams waiting to be served, resulting in unsatisfactory user channel quality and long queuing delay. In response, we formulated a multi-beam placement problem to jointly optimize beam placement and utilization efficiency of satellite resources. Then we proposed an algorithm based on density clustering to solve the problem and assign all users to different beam footprints according to their geographic location with low complexity. Each beam footprint will be served by a beam according to the BH schedule afterwards. Finally we present the evaluation of the proposed scheme from different aspects. Simulation results indicate that compared with other benchmark schemes, the proposed one is more superior in improving the system throughput and reducing the average queuing delay.

articleTitle: Hybrid Precoding with Low-Resolution PSs for URLLC users in Cell-Free MmWave MIMO Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel probability learning approach based on cross entropy (CE) to design the hybrid precoding with low-resolution phase shifters (PS) for URLLC users in a cell-free massive MIMO system. Based on the finite blocklength transmission, we construct a fairness optimization problem with the objective of maximizing the worst user’s achievable rate and minimizing the worst user’s decoding error probability successively. This kind of mixed integer programming problem is difficult to solve with traditional convex optimization, and the processing time is too long to meet the low delay requirements of URLLC due to the high complexity in cell-free systems. However, the CE-based approach we proposed can synchronously design the precoding of all distributed RRUs, adopting a parallel computing framework, and it greatly reduces processing latency, which is very friendly to URLLC service.

articleTitle: An Improved Newton-Schulz Iterative Algorithm for Massive MIMO Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: The exact matrix inversion required by the conventional minimum mean square error (MMSE) detector for massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) brings unaffordable computational burden that hinders efficient implementation. In this paper, a linear iterative detector based on Newton-Schulz algorithm is proposed to avoid the inversion of MMSE. An initialization scheme and a successive-update schedule is proposed to enhance the convergence rate and accuracy of the Newton-Schulz detector. Simulation results are illustrated to show that the proposed detector can approach the bit-error-rate (BER) performance of MMSE with reduced complexity. Moreover, it can outperform state-of-the-art (SOA) linear detection methods under various MIMO scenarios.

articleTitle: Research on High-speed Detection Method of Radar Signal Based on RFSoC
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: This paper proposes a real-time radar signal detection method based on RFSoC and parallel Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) architecture, suitable for electronic warfare (EW) applications in electronic reconnaissance aircraft. The proposed method utilizes high-speed Analog-to-Digital Converters (ADC) and high-performance heterogeneous processing units integrated in RFSoC, combined with parallel FFT algorithm, to optimize the radar signal detection architecture. It improves the time-accuracy trade-off in large point FFT processing, enabling the electronic reconnaissance aircraft to detect radar signals containing any number of carriers with instantaneous bandwidth of 2 GHz and frequency resolution of 1 MHz in 3 us. Both Matlab simulation and real-world experimental results are presented to validate the rationality and reliability of the design, providing a reference for the design of modern high-performance electronic reconnaissance aircraft.

articleTitle: Joint Blind Channel Estimation, Activity Detection, and Decoding for Coded Massive Random Access
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: A signal scrambling based joint blind channel estimation, activity detection, and data decoding (SS-JCAD) scheme is proposed for coded massive random access systems. The signal scrambling, which is a symbol-wise phase rotation to each user’s modulated data, has no bandwidth expansion and energy consumption. Yet, with it, each user’s channel state information (CSI), including both the user’s active status and channel coefficient, is blindly detected by a low-complexity single-user maximum a posteriori estimation without the help of pilots. With the estimated CSI as a prior, a soft parallel interference cancellation based multi-user decoding is performed. A soft information iteration algorithm between the channel estimation and multi-user decoding is developed to improve the reliability of both. Simulation shows that for massive random access systems with system load less than 1.5, SS-JCAD achieves almost the same bit error rate as the ideal case that perfect CSI is available, implying SS-JCAD as a near-optimal solution to the random access problem.

Author Keywords: joint channel estimation and multi-user decoding

articleTitle: Constructions of Girth-Eight QC-LDPC Codes with Dual-Diagonal Structure Based on GCD Framework
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: A novel class of quasi-cyclic (QC) low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes is explicitly proposed without 4-cycles and 6-cycles via the greatest-common-divisor (GCD) framework. From the new codes, a novel type of girth-eight QC-LDPC codes with a dual-diagonal (DD) structure is presented, in which the single undetermined entry in the associated exponent matrix can be determined by simple formulae. The proposed DD codes have similar or better performance compared with DD codes obtained from computer search. Moreover, a lower bound on circulant sizes which guarantees the existence of qualified undetermined entries is also provided.

articleTitle: Clutter-Aware MIMO-OFDM Based Target Detection: Algorithm Design and Experimental Test
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Wireless sensing aided by well-established communication systems is an important research direction in the area of integrated sensing and communications (ISAC). In this work, we investigate the clutter-aware target detection based on the commonly used multiple-input multiple-output orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (MIMO-OFDM) communication framework. Specifically, under the premise that the clutter covariance matrix is unknown, we develop two generalized likelihood ratio test (GLRT) based detection methods for the scenarios with unknown and known noise variance, respectively. We adopt practical fifth-generation (5G) new radio (NR) frames to perform both simulation and experiment, which show that the proposed methods yield remarkable performance gains compared to the traditional energy detector. Furthermore, when the noise variance is known, the proposed detector exhibits near-optimal performance.

Author Keywords: multiple-input multiple-output orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (MIMO-OFDM)

articleTitle: Anti-Eavesdropping in UAV Secure Communications: Joint Trajectory and Power Allocation Optimization with Two-Way Training
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: This paper investigates an unmanned ariel vehicle (UAV)-enabled secure communication system, where an UAV sends confidential information to legitimate ground users (LGUs) in the presence of a ground eavesdropper (Eve). In order to improve the comprehensive security performance of UAV network communication, a two-way training-based discriminatory channel estimation (DCE) scheme focusing on physical layer security (PLS) is proposed. We derive the closed-form expression of the average secrecy rate (ASR) and the minimum normalized mean square error (NMSE). On the premise of ensuring the effectiveness of channel estimation errors, we aim to maximize the ASR of the system, by jointly optimizing the UAV’s flight trajectory and power allocation. Due to the intractability of the formulated problem, block coordinate descent (BCD) and successive convex approximation (SCA) techniques are applied to solve the problem. Numerical results show that the proposed scheme can enhance the security of the UAV communication. Moreover, the relationship between system ASR and UAV power allocation is revealed.

articleTitle: Sensing and Beamtracking Scheme Design for UAV-Enabled ISAC Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In the unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-enabled systems, beamtracking is an important design issue. In this paper, we leverage the benefits of the integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) techniques to improve the beamtracking performance in the UAV-enabled systems. Specifically, we first obtain the angle-of-arrival/angle-of-departure (AoA/AoD) from the echo signals. Using the estimated angular information, we then propose an improved unscented Kalman filter (UKF)-based beamtracking scheme to predict the AoA/AoD from past information, taking the mobility of the UAV and the large accumulative estimation error of conventional UKF-based beamtracking scheme into account. Through numerical results, we show that our proposed beamtracking scheme can accurately estimate the AoA/AoD of our considered systems. We also demonstrate how our proposed scheme can be utilized to achieve nearly the same signal-to-noise ratio performance compared to the baseline assuming perfect AoA/AoD estimation.

articleTitle: Outage Probability Analysis of RIS-Assisted Relay Transmission Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: This paper investigates the outage performance of a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted relay transmission network consisting of a source, a destination, multiple decode-and-forward (DF) relays, and a RIS, where the RIS assists in the source-to-relay and relay-to-destination transmissions. We propose two RIS-assisted relay selection schemes, namely the RIS-assisted round-robin scheduling (RIS-RRS) scheme and the RIS-assisted opportunistic relay selection (RIS-ORS) scheme. We analyze closed-form expressions of outage probabilities (OPs) for the RIS-RRS and RIS-ORS schemes and also carry out the minimization of the OPs to enhance outage performance through the optimization of RIS deployment location. It is shown that the proposed RIS-assisted relay selection achieves better outage performance than the conventional relay selection without RIS and RIS-aided source transmission without relays. Moreover, the RIS-ORS scheme generally outperforms the RIS-RRS scheme in terms of the outage probability. Additionally, numerical results show that the OPs of RIS-RRS and RIS-ORS schemes can be further reduced by adjusting the RIS deployment location.

articleTitle: RIS-Assisted Coded Relay Cooperation Based on LDPC Product Codes with Finite Code Length
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) is a kind of metamaterial with the ability to regulate and control wireless channels, which can provide additional links for wireless communication systems. Meanwhile, it has low hardware cost, low energy consumption, flexible deployment, and intelligent reconfiguration merits. By combining the RIS technology with coded relay cooperation, we establish the RIS-assisted coded relay cooperation based on low density parity check (LDPC) product codes, and further propose the LDPC product code encoding method and efficient joint iterative decoding algorithm. Then, we theoretically derive the approximate solutions of the outage probability and the channel capacity with finite code length. Theoretical analysis and simulation results show that the proposed system obviously outperforms the traditional coded relay cooperation, and the more number of RIS elements, the more significant advantage can be obtained. Simulation results also demonstrate that the channel capacity with finite code length approaches the ideal channel capacity with the code length of LDPC product codes increasing.

Author Keywords: channel capacity with finite code length

articleTitle: Multi-Class Image Generation from EEG Features with Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Exploring the visual coding mechanism of the human brain has been an important topic in brain-computer interface technology, holding the potential to provide new insights into the research of the Internet of Things (IoT). Especially, the use of brain signals for image generation has attracted people’s attention. In this paper, we propose a multi-class image generation method based on electroencephalography (EEG) features with conditional generative adversarial networks (CGAN). Specifically, we synchronously collect the EEG signals when subjects watch visual stimuli through EEG equipment and construct a multi-category image-EEG dataset. The obtained EEG dataset undergoes preprocessing to eliminate interference from electrooculographic signals and electromyographic signals. Based on this dataset, we extract EEG features related to visual stimuli by deep learning algorithms and integrate them with CGAN for image generation. We employ different EEG feature extraction methods for image generation and conduct comparative experiments. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method based on the CGAN model utilizing the joint EEG spatio-temporal and temporal-frequency features can achieve better performance in the image generation task.

articleTitle: Periodic Shifting Semi-Persistent Scheduling for Multi-User Communication in 5G-TSN Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: With the development of industrial automation, the flexible communication systems with deterministic capabilities are more essential now than ever before. Given that the high flexibility of 5G and the determinacy of Time-Sensitive Networking (TSN), the integration of 5G and TSN (5G-TSN) is expected to provide flexible and deterministic communications for the industry. However, traditional Semi-Persistent Scheduling (SPS) techniques fail to meet the requirements of periodic and time-sensitive traffic due to periodicity misalignment between resource assignments and arriving packets in the temporal domain. For high scheduling precision, this paper develop a novel Periodic Shifting SPS (NPS-SPS) for multi-user Time Sensitive Communication (TSC), which recursively adjusts the scheduling period of reserved resource assignments jointly with the resource block allocation to reduce the misalignment delay. Performance evaluation shows that compared with the existing scheme the proposed approach can reduce the latency by about 40%.

articleTitle: Quantum Network Coding Based on Quantum Steering
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Quantum steering is a physical resource that has important application value in quantum information. Quantum network coding provides an alternative solution for quantum-state distribution, especially when the bottleneck problems must be considered and high communication speed is required. In this paper, we introduce quantum steering into quantum network coding, and propose a feasible quantum network coding scheme to transmit any of the four quantum states in butterfly networks. By only using the steerable property, we make an attempt to relax the restriction on entangled quantum pairs to quantum steering.

articleTitle: A Scheduling-based Hybrid Medium Access Control Protocol for Underwater Acoustic Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Designing a media access control (MAC) protocol for underwater acoustic sensor networks (UASNs) related to application scenario is widely researched recently.
