From the perspective of data transmission characteristics of distributed data collection task via UASNs, a hybrid MAC protocol with centralized scheduling and distributed scheduling strategies is proposed in this paper. In the proposed MAC protocol, two scheduling strategies, namely the centralized scheduling for sensor nodes with periodic data and the distributed scheduling strategy for sensor nodes with intermittent data. And the scheduling strategy used by a sensor node is determined by its data rate. Moreover, the proportion of resource allocated for the centralized scheduling and the distributed scheduling is determined by the sink node according to the network load. Moreover, to improve channel utilization, specific control packets are designed to replace handshake packet interaction. Simulation results show that the proposed MAC protocol outperforms in terms of network throughput, end-to-end delay, packet delivery ratio, and energy consumption.

articleTitle: Channel Truncation Inspired Short-Packet Covert Communication with Poisson Packet Generation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In this paper, we consider short-packet covert communications with Poisson packet generation. To guarantee an optimal prior transmission probability while improving the communication reliability, we propose a novel covert communication scheme based on the channel truncation transmission. For the proposed scheme, we derive close-form expressions for the lower bound on covertness constraint, the average packet error probability, and the effective covert throughput (ECT). Then, the transmit power and the channel truncation threshold are jointly optimized to maximize ECT, while the close-form expression for the optimal channel truncation threshold with a given transmit power is obtained. Our examination shows the superiority of the proposed transmission scheme relative to a benchmark scheme without channel truncation in terms of achieving a higher ECT.

articleTitle: An Efficient Beamforming Design for Near-Field Beam Squint Mitigation in Wideband ELAA Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In the future 6G wireless networks, the growing number of antennas and extra-wide mmWave frequency band will lead to near-field effect and beam squint effect. The generated beams at different frequencies will respectively focused at different locations referred to as the near-field beam squint effect, which will cause a severe performance degradation, remaining to be mitigated efficiently to enhance the data rates. We propose an efficient grouping beamforming design algorithm utilizing the near-field codebook to generate the analog beamformer. Specifically, we uniformly partition the entire large array into multiple small subarrays and design the beamforming of each subarray for the specific selected subcarrier in the whole bandwidth. The analog beamformer and digital beamformer are iteratively designed until a convergence solution is obtained. Simulation results illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach to mitigate near-field beam squint effect.

articleTitle: Reliability Performance of STAR-RIS Aided NOMA Short-Packet Communications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: This paper investigates the reliability performance of a downlink simultaneous transmitting and reflecting reconfigurable intelligent surface (STAR-RIS) enabled non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) network with short packet communications. In the considered network, two blocked users communicate with the aid of STAR-RIS and transmit by utilizing the energy spitting protocol. To characterize the performance, the closedform expressions of average block error rate (BLER) at the users are derived and diversity order is also analyzed. The theoretical analysis is verified through simulation results. The achieved results demonstrate that the proposed STAR-RIS-NOMA network outperforms the conventional RIS-NOMA and relay schemes in terms of reliability performance.

articleTitle: Semantic Communication for Cooperative Perception Based on the Importance Map
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Cooperative perception, which has a broader perception field than single-vehicle perception, has played an increasingly important role in autonomous driving to conduct 3D object detection. Through vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) communication technology, various connected automated vehicles (CAVs) can share their sensory information (LiDAR point clouds) for cooperative perception. We employ an importance map to extract significant semantic information and propose a novel cooperative perception semantic communication scheme with intermediate fusion. Meanwhile, our proposed architecture can be extended to the challenging time-varying multi-path fading channel. To alleviate the distortion caused by the time-varying multi-path fading, we adopt orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) blocks combined with channel estimation and channel equalization. Simulation results demonstrate that our proposed model outperforms the traditional separate source-channel coding over various channel models.

articleTitle: Enhanced Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface-Aided Amplitude Phase Shift Keying
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In this paper, we put forth an enhanced reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-aided amplitude phase shift keying (APSK) modulation scheme. In the proposed scheme, the RIS elements that are partitioned into multiple groups generate APSK-modulated signals by illuminating an RIS with unmodulated carrier waves and by adjusting the on/off states and phase shifts of the RIS groups according to the information to be transmitted. Different from the existing RIS-APSK, the proposed scheme changes the initial phase shift of the RIS groups when an even number of RIS groups are active, thus enlarging the minimum Euclidean distance of the APSK constellation. Two maximum-likelihood (ML) detectors that respectively use instantaneous and statistic channel state information are developed for the proposed scheme, and closed-form upper bounds on the symbol error rates are derived for both ML detectors. Moreover, we design two low-complexity detectors, which detect the phase first and the amplitude first, respectively. Simulation results show the superiority of the proposed scheme over the existing RIS-APSK and RIS-PSK.

articleTitle: Rotational Misalignment Compensation for Underwater Optical Wireless Communication Employing Quaternary Polarization Shift Keying Modulation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In an underwater optical wireless communication (UOWC) system employing quaternary polarization shift keying (QPolSK) modulation, the rotational misalignment due to relative rotation of a transmitter and a receiver leads to drastic performance degradation. This work first presents an algorithm for estimating the deviation angle by leveraging the rotational invariance of circular polarization modulation. Then two rotational misalignment compensation methods employing digital signal processing and mechanical rotation respectively are introduced. Their feasibility is experimentally verified, and their respective features are discussed. The results indicate that their joint deployment can potentially deal with a large range of rotational misalignment.

articleTitle: MIMO Detection Based on Graph Neural Network with Belief Propagation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Graph neural network (GNN) has been considered for massive multiple-inputmultiple-output (MIMO) detection recently due to its strong capability in solving graph-based classification problems. However, current GNN detectors still struggle between performance and complexity under high order modulations. In this paper, we propose a novel GNN-based MIMO detector named GNN-BP, which combines GNN and belief propagation (BP) messages. The GNN is constructed based on the Markov random field (MRF) MIMO model, while extra node features are introduced from BP as a supplement to effectively enhance the detection performance with acceptable extra cost. Simulation results show that the proposed GNN-BP detector can outperform state-of-the-art (SOA) GNN-based detectors, and achieves similar performance as GNN with expectation propagation (GEP) with much lower computational cost.

articleTitle: A Novel Unsupervised Learning Network for Direction-of-Arrival Estimation in Internet of Things Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Unsupervised learning is an emerging technique in the field of signal processing that allows for autonomous feature learning without reliance on annotated data. In this paper, we propose a novel unsupervised learning network to address the challenges of Direction-of-Arrival (DoA) estimation in indoor localization for the Internet of Things (IoT). Our focus is on resolving the issue of inadequate DoA estimation performance in complex scenarios. The proposed network is based on a multilayer and multi-path feature extraction approach. We employ a multi-layer feature extraction approach to separately extract general and specialized features, and then implement multi-path feature extraction to extract different parameters. Through the design of multi-layer and multi-path, we can improve the estimation performance of the network. In addition, considering the impact of noise on the estimation performance of the network, we devise a novel decoding scheme in the decoder module, further enhancing the performance of the network. Simulation results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed method over existing approaches in terms of DoA estimation performance.

articleTitle: Cloud-Edge Collaborative Human Activity Recognition System Design and Implementation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: This paper proposes an edge computing architecture for Human Activity Recognition (HAR) based on Raspberry Pi and HaaS100, aimed at enhancing real-time performance and system robustness. The proposed approach employs Edge-End inference within the communication range of edge nodes, while relying on Cloud Edge inference otherwise, thereby establishing a comprehensive Cloud Edge End system that leverages the capabilities of a mobile communication 5G private network Wi-Fi. To achieve accurate activity recognition, three algorithms, namely Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), CNN-Long Short-Term Memory (CNN-LSTM), and Residual Network-based CNN (ResNet-based CNN), are implemented and their performances are rigorously compared using Actitracker datasets. The experimental results demonstrate that the ResNet-based CNN exhibits superior performance, achieving an impressive F1-score of 0.977. Additionally, to address the challenge of model size and resource-constrained edge devices, model compression is employed through channel-wise data collection, effectively reducing the parameter size from 220,000 to 160,000, with a negligible 0.5% decrease in accuracy. Finally, the compressed model is deployed on edge devices, and retraining is conducted using self-collected datasets to ensure practicality and adaptability in real-world scenarios. The proposed HAR edge computing architecture showcases significant advancements in real-time performance, system robustness, and resource optimization, making it a promising solution for activity recognition in edge computing environments.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Integrated Sensing and Communication Waveform Based on LFM-CPM
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: The integrated waveform of sensing and communication is to overlap the sensing waveform and the communication waveform in the time and frequency domains, and respectively perform radar signal processing and communication signal processing at the receiving end. The integrated waveform obtained by superimposing the linear frequency modulated (LFM) signal and the continuous phase modulated (CPM) signal has the property of constant envelope, which can effectively avoid the signal distortion caused by the nonlinearity of the power amplifier, so it has better sensing performance and communication performance. In this paper, a new multi-segment frame structure design is proposed to solve the problem of spectral spreading of LFM-CPM waveforms, and comprehensively considers synchronization acquisition, the estimation and recovery of frequency offset and phase offset. In addition, we propose an efficient implementation of integrated waveforms based on FPGA, which can reduce resource consumption and improve quantization accuracy. Finally, we complete the designed integrated system on the hardware platform, and the experimental results show that the sensing and communication performances are outstanding.

articleTitle: Resnet-Conformer Network using Multi-Scale Channel Attention for Sound Event Localization and Detection in Real Scenes
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Sound Event Localization and Detection (SELD) aims at detecting the class and activity time of the sound events, while estimating their corresponding direction of arrival (DOA). The difficulties of SELD lie in the change of acoustic scenes and the presence of overlapping sound events. To improve the performance of SELD, in this work, we propose a Resnet-Conformer network based on multi-scale channel attention (MSCA-RCnet) to conduct SELD. To that end, first, we take the RCnet as the backbone of the model and add the multi-scale channel attention (MSCA) to the Resnet block to capture channel-level dependencies. Second, we utilize attentive statistics pooling (ASP) to resolve the mismatch between label resolution and frame-level feature temporal resolution and enhance the discriminability of the features. Finally, we integrate the MSCA-RCnet and the Event-Independent Network V2 (EINV2) by multi-ACCDOA representation into an EINV2-based multi-ACCDOA network. Subsequently, we perform an average ensemble of these two models. To address the shortage of training data, we employ audio channel swapping (ACS) and AugMix to the dataset. Finally, we evaluate our proposed systems in the Audio-only Track of the DCASE 2023 Task 3 and rank the second place in the competition.

articleTitle: Adaptive Bitrate Video Semantic Communication over Wireless Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: This paper investigates the adaptive bitrate (ABR) video semantic communication over wireless networks. In the considered model, video sensing devices must transmit video semantic information to an edge server, to facilitate ubiquitous video sensing services such as road environment monitoring at the edge server in autonomous driving scenario. However, due to the varying wireless network conditions, it is challenging to guarantee both low transmission delay and high semantic accuracy at the same time if devices continuously transmit a fixed bitrate video semantic information. To address this challenge, we develop an adaptive bitrate video semantic communication (ABRVSC) system, in which devices adaptively adjust the bitrate of video semantic information according to network conditions. Specifically, we first define the quality of experience (QoE) for video semantic communication. Subsequently, a swin transformer-based semantic codec is proposed to extract semantic information with considering the influence of QoE. Then, we propose an Actor-Critic based ABR algorithm for the semantic codec to enhance the robustness of the proposed ABRVSC scheme against network variations. Simulation results demonstrate that at low bitrates, the mean intersection over union (MIoU) of the proposed ABRVSC scheme is nearly twice that of the traditional scheme. Moreover, the proposed ABRVSC scheme, which increases the QoE in video semantic communication by 36.57%, exhibits more robustness against network variations compared to both the fixed bitrate schemes and traditional ABR schemes.

articleTitle: Traffic-Aware Hierarchical Beam Selection for Cell-Free Massive MIMO
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Beam selection for joint transmission in cell-free massive multi-input multi-output systems faces the problem of extremely high training overhead and computational complexity. The traffic-oriented quality of service additionally complicates the beam selection problem. To address this issue, we propose a traffic-aware hierarchical beam selection scheme performed in a dual timescale. In the long-timescale, the central processing unit collects wide beam responses from base stations (BSs) to predict the power profile in the narrow beamspace with a convolutional neural network, based on which the cascaded multiple-BS beamspace is carefully pruned. In the short-timescale, maximization of delay satisfaction rate w.r.t. beam selections within multiple consecutive time slots is modeled as a partially observable Markov decision process (POMDP) and addressed by reinforcement learning. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed scheme significantly reduces both model training cost and beam training overhead and is more likely to meet the user-specific delay requirement, compared to existing methods.

articleTitle: Semantic Segmentation Aided Image Transmission for Maritime UAV Surveillance Network
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In maritime surveillance networks, limited energy consumption resources and long delays are serious issues that deteriorate the performance of image transmission for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). Therefore, in this paper, we provide a task-transfer UAV system based on hybrid networks and a semantic segmentation-aided image transmission scheme. Our work mainly includes three aspects. Firstly, we compare the image reconstruction quality and transmission delay of our proposed technique to those of traditional image transmission schemes. Secondly, the energy consumption of the task-transfer UAV system based on hybrid networks is compared to that of the single-network UAV system. Finally, an energy consumption optimization model is established for the task-transfer UAV system based on hybrid networks under delay and bandwidth constraints. The experimental results show that the proposed image transmission scheme can achieve better anti-noise performance and less latency, and our task-transfer UAV system based on hybrid networks uses less energy on average, which is more suitable for multi-task demand scenarios. In addition, by adjusting the bandwidth of the task-transfer UAV system based on hybrid networks, the energy consumption of the transmission system can be further reduced.

articleTitle: Constructing MDS Array Codes with Small Repair Bandwidth under Sub-packetization Two
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Erasure Codes are widely implemented in distributed storage systems to achieve fault tolerance with high storage efficiency. Reed-Solomon code is commonly deployed in data centers due to its optimal storage efficiency, but it requires massive repair bandwidth for node repair. Minimum Storage Regenerating (MSR) code and Locally Repairable (LR) code are proposed to reduce repair bandwidth. However, MSR code usually carries a heavy disk I/O burden and LR code is not optimal in storage efficiency. In this paper, we take disk I/O, storage efficiency, repair bandwidth, sub-packetization level, and repair degree (number of helper nodes) into consideration together, and propose explicit construction of MDS array code (named LDIO code) with low disk I/O and reduced repair bandwidth, where the sub-packetization level is 2. Besides the low disk I/O consumption, LDIO code also achieves a small repair bandwidth of ${\bar \gamma _{sys}} = \frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{{4(r - 1)}}$ for systematic nodes with repair degree d = k+1. Normally, LDIO code can provide bandwidth savings of 25% to 50% for the repair of systematic nodes compared with RS code, and almost savings of 6% compared with piggybacking code. For an LDIO code of length n and redundancy r, the size of the finite field needed is Θ(n<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r+1</sup>).

articleTitle: Hybrid Beamforming Design for MIMO-ISAC Systems via Consensus-ADMM
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Hybrid analog-digital beamforming has been identified as an attractive technology, since it is able to effectively reduce hardware cost without significantly reducing the system performance, especially in large-scale antenna array systems. In this paper, we consider the problem of hybrid beamforming design for multi-user multiple-input multiple-output integrated sensing and communication (MIMO-ISAC) systems. The problem for the design is formulated as maximizing the minimum transmit energy radiated towards the region-of-interest (ROI) for sensing, subject to the signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) constraints of communication users, unimodular constraints of the analog beamformer phase shifters as well as the total transmission power constraint. To deal with the challenging nonconvex problem, an algorithm based on the consensus alternation direction method of multipliers (CADMM) is developed. Different from the existing two-stage algorithm for such designs, where in general the SINR constraint cannot be satisfied, in the proposed method this constraint is considered during the iterations, so that the SINR requirements can be always guaranteed. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

Author Keywords: consensus alternating direction method of multipliers (CADMM)

articleTitle: Decentralized Adaptive Formation via Consensus-Oriented Multi-Agent Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Adaptive multi-agent formation control, which requires the formation to flexibly adjust along with the quantity variations of agents in a decentralized manner, belongs to one of the most challenging issues in multi-agent systems, especially under communication-limited constraints. In this paper, we propose a novel Consensus-based Decentralized Adaptive Formation (Cons-DecAF) framework. Specifically, we develop a novel multi-agent reinforcement learning method, Consensus-oriented Multi-Agent Communication (ConsMAC), to enable agents to perceive global information and establish the consensus from local states by effectively aggregating neighbor messages. Afterwards, we leverage policy distillation to accomplish the adaptive formation adjustment. Meanwhile, instead of pre-assigning specific positions of agents, we employ a displacement-based formation by Hausdorff distance to significantly improve the formation efficiency. The experimental results through extensive simulations validate that the proposed method has achieved outstanding performance in terms of both speed and stability.

articleTitle: Channel Domain Anti-Jamming based on Multi-Active Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Existing anti-jamming technologies mainly focus on communication signal space, such as frequency hopping and direct sequence spread spectrum. Inspired by the significant advantages of Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS), and in order to overcome "double fading", multi-active RISs were proposed to explore the communication channel space to anti-jamming in this paper. Specifically, a dynamic heterogeneous redundant channel model was constructed based on multiactive RISs, and a channel domain anti-jamming algorithm was proposed. Firstly, the uncertain jamming information is robustly processed, and the cyclic coordinate descent (CCD) and successive convex approximation (SCA) are used to optimize RISs phase shift matrix and amplitude matrix, respectively. Besides, the closed form solutions of the transmitting beam and the receiving beam are obtained. Secondly, the low complexity algorithm of block coordinate descent (BCD) is used to alternately optimize the above variables. Finally, the greedy algorithm is used to switch and regulate the multiple RISs. Theoretical analysis and simulation results show that the proposed method can effectively improve communication rate under the condition of significant uncertainty of jamming.

articleTitle: User Scheduling and Height Optimization in UAV-Assisted Maritime XL-MIMO Communications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: As an important part of the space-air-ground-sea integrated communication networks, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) have recently garnered considerable attention. In this paper, we consider the UAV-assisted user scheduling and height optimization in the maritime extremely large-scale multiple-input-multiple-output system. To improve the achievable sum-rate, we focus on reducing inter-channel interference by optimizing the USV positions and the UAV-base station (BS) height. Specifically, we derive a set of orthogonal positions in the near-field region of the uniform rectangular array such that the channels of the USVs located at that positions are orthogonal to each other. Based on the orthogonal positions, we propose a joint optimization algorithm that provides a suboptimal orthogonal position assignment scheme for the USVs and optimizes the UAV-BS height. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed orthogonal position and the joint optimization algorithm.

articleTitle: A Channel Robust Radio Frequency Fingerprint Authentication Method Based on Hadamard Product Comparison
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Radio Frequency Fingerprinting (RFF) is an emerging identification technology that utilizes wireless signals to identify specific devices. Due to the presence of variable channel conditions in practical applications, designing channel-robust RFF techniques is a challenging task. This paper proposes a channel-robust RFF authentication method, which implements the authentication function by comparing the Hadamard product results of two different fixed signal segments. In order to further mitigate the impact of variable channel conditions on authentication results, a windowed Channel Impulse Response (CIR) compensation method is also utilized in this paper. Taking the IEEE 802.11 system as an example, the experiment uses 4 Wi-Fi routers of the same model and production batch in three different scenarios: indoor static, indoor mobile, and outdoor corridors. Using the original data comparison method, the average accuracy rate exceeds 95%, and it can be further improved by 1% to 2% after the windowed CIR compensation. Moreover, using only one frame as reference data, this approach can also achieve approximately 95% authentication accuracy.

articleTitle: Joint Multicast Transmission and Channel Allocation Strategy for Data Dissemination in Vehicular Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: The prosperity of advanced applications in vehicular networks leads to frequent data requests of vehicles, necessitating an increased emphasis on data dissemination capabilities. Multicast transmission, enabling the simultaneous delivery of data to multiple receivers, stands out as a spectrally efficient approach for data dissemination. However, existing approaches in multicast transmission strategy for vehicular networks largely ignore the interference that can arise between multicast links, which results in a degradation of system performance. In this paper, we investigate the issue of joint multicast transmission and bandwidth allocation strategy for enhancing data dissemination in vehicular networks and formulate a problem to maximize the number of packets effectively transmitted by optimizing multicast link establishment, transmitted packets and bandwidth allocation. Because of the coupling of variables in the formulated problem, we decompose the problem into two subproblems and propose the conflict graph based multicast transmission strategy and the graph coloring algorithm based bandwidth allocation strategy for each subproblem. Then, an iterative algorithm is designed for joint optimization. Extensive simulations demonstrate the advantages of proposed strategy.

articleTitle: Partial Replication-Enabled Cooperative Transmission for Distributed Edge Computing
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: With the proliferation of delay-sensitive and computation-intensive mobile applications, recent years have witnessed a transition towards more advanced distributed edge computing. However, the diverse computation results among different edge nodes (ENs) in conventional distributed edge computing present challenges to cooperative transmission and may result in prolonged downlink latency. In this regard, replicated edge computing has emerged as a promising solution to perform computations repeatedly across multiple ENs, thereby facilitating cooperative transmission in the downlink. Nonetheless, this approach inevitably leads to additional computation cost. To encompass the advantages of both distributed edge computing and replicated edge computing, a novel partial replication based distributed edge computing is proposed in this work. Specifically, by partitioning the original task into a common part computed at all ENs and multiple private parts, with each computed by one EN, cooperative downlink transmission can be enabled without incurring excessive computation cost. To minimize the overall processing delay, a task partition and downlink transmit power allocation algorithm is developed based on alternating optimization. Simulation results are presented to validate the superiority of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: DNAT: Multi-scale Transformer with Dilated Neighborhood Attention for Image Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Recently, Transformer-based models have achieved remarkable progress for image classification. In order to reduce the computational costs of multi-head self-attention (MHSA) that is widely adopted in recently-proposed visual Transformers, some window-based Transformers employ local self-attention via shrinking number of input tokens. Nevertheless, these approaches to some extent are short to model long-range dependencies. To address this problem, this paper presents an effective and powerful Transformer backbone, called Dilated Neighborhood Attention Transformer (DNAT) that has a mutli-path architecture, for image classification. DNAT is able to explore long-range interactions through dilated neighborhood attention (DNA). When dilation rate is small, DNAT degenerates to local self-attention that is computationally efficient to capture local features. As the dilation rate increases, more and more long-range token interactions are explored step-by-step. Finally, by integrating weighted features derived from various dilation rates, DNAT seamlessly harvests local-to-global context, yet with acceptable growth of model size and computational budgets. The extensive experiments on ImageNet-1K and CIFAR100 datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of DNAT for image classification.

articleTitle: EoSI-Aware Resource Allocation for Semantic Communication-Enabled Industrial IoT System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In the semantic communication-enabled Industrial Internet of Things system (SemCom-IIoT), ensuring efficient task accomplishment encounters a critical issue: how to timely and accurately transmit and process semantic information of moderate amount with minimum resource cost, namely improving the efficiency of semantic information applied to the task. To overcome the problem, we provide a joint optimization of multi-dimensional resource allocation and semantic retention ratio selection in this paper. Specifically, a novel performance metric named efficiency of semantic information (EoSI) is defined to quantify the aforementioned efficiency. Further, considering the dynamics of the industrial environment, we exploit a deep reinforcement learning algorithm to maximize EoSI of the system by adaptively adjusting the allocation of computing resources, bandwidth resources and the selection of semantic retention ratio. Extensive simulation results demonstrate that our proposed approach can significantly enhance EoSI by up to 173% and 139% respectively in the context of a large number of devices and the strict task accuracy requirement, compared with other benchmarks.

articleTitle: Automatic Radio Map Updating with Multi-Scale Feature for Wireless Indoor Localization
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: The accuracy of fingerprint-based indoor localization strongly relates to the precision of the wireless radio map. However, radio maps are vulnerable to deployment changes and require constant maintenance, which is labor-intensive and time-consuming. To address this issue, we propose an automated radio map update method that employs a mobile robot to collect fingerprints along its path. Considering the relationship between signal strength and propagation distance, we design a reconstruction network combining multi-scale features in radio map updating, which estimates signal strengths based on local and global distributions. In addition, we propose a dynamic strategy with an attention mechanism to select a set of crucial representative points (RPs) for a sparse survey in the update stage. The chosen points have stronger relations to the surroundings than other points, improving our method’s reconstruction accuracy. The experimental results show that the proposed method reconstructs the radio maps of our two test sites which outperforms the state-of-art approaches in reconstruction accuracy by 32.03%. And the localization accuracy of the updated radio maps is significantly improved by about 51.39%.

articleTitle: Hierarchical Federated Learning for Collaborative Caching in Fog Computing
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: With the rapid development of 5G/BG technologies, the wireless communication system faces significant bottleneck in terms of both latency and throughput. The fog computing network is an emerging computing model aimed at expanding the capabilities and performance of cloud computing, while providing lower latency and higher reliability. Therefore, fog network cache technology has emerged as a promising solution to reduce latency base on more efficient computing and data processing capabilities. Moreover, in the fog computing network, most of the existing learning methods are based on the centralized learning, which poses the risk of privacy leakage in data sharing. To address the above challenges, in this paper, we propose a three-layer fog network which consists of cloud layer, fog layer, and user layer for the content caching. Moreover, hierarchical federated learning (HFL) is employed to train a deep neural network (DNN) model to predict the content popularity while mitigating the privacy risks by exchanging models rather than the historical raw data. Additionally, a collaborative content caching method based on the caching value is designed to maximize the overall content caching value, reduce the cache redundancy and minimize the content acquisition latency. Finally, the simulation results demonstrate the efficiency and performance of the HFL-based collaborative content caching algorithm.

articleTitle: A Non-Stationary Channel Emulator for 6G THz Wireless Channels
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: To facilitate the deployment of terahertz (THz) communication systems, it is crucial to develop a channel emulator to accurately and reliably evaluate their performance, which can provide a controlled and repeatable channel environment. However, a suitable channel emulator generating a three-dimensional (3D) non-stationary sixth generation (6G) THz geometry-based stochastic model (GBSM) is missing. To construct this emulator, we utilize a field-programmable gate array (FPGA) development platform to enable the construction of a frequency domain non-stationary THz channel emulator. The channel emulator uses band stitching based on the sum of frequency-modulation (SoFM), along with a sine generation algorithm based on the coordinate rotating digital computer (CORDIC). These techniques guarantee the generation of the THz ultra-wideband (UWB) fading channels. We evaluate the performance of the channel emulator by comparing its important statistical properties, such as the frequency correlation function (FCF), spatial cross-correlation function (SCCF), temporal autocorrelation function (TACF), and cumulative distribution function (CDF) of the stationary bandwidth, with the corresponding theoretical channel model. The proposed channel emulator shows good performance.

articleTitle: Design of Intelligent Reflecting Surface-Assisted Wireless Computational Imaging
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Wireless imaging, as a typical method of wireless sensing, is a promising application of the sixth generation (6G) wireless networks. In particular, radio-frequency signals originally dedicated to communication are also used for imaging without extra detectors or sensors. Wireless imaging usually suffers from channel fading, interference and noise, resulting in low imaging accuracy. Hence, advanced signal processing approaches are employed to enhance the imaging performance, namely wireless computational imaging (WCI). In this paper, we propose to utilize intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) to further improve the performance of WCI in complex environments. By minimizing the mean square error (MSE) of the reflectivity of interested physical object, we design a reflection matrix optimization algorithm for IRS. Both theoretical analysis and simulation results show the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm for WCI in 6G cellular Internet of Things (IoT).

articleTitle: Deployment Optimization of Multi-UAV Network for Low Delay Maritime Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Deploying unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) as relay nodes to connect ships on the sea with base stations (BS) on the ground is a promising solution in future maritime communications. In this paper, we propose a low-delay UAV deployment(LDUD) algorithm to cover all ships on a given area of the sea, aims to minimize the number of UAVs and the data transmission delay from ships to BS. The LDUD algorithm includes two sub-algorithms: the first one is a coverage algorithm based on convex hull (CACH) and the second one is a network formation game combined with virtual force (NFVF). In the first sub-algorithm, a UAV network with minimum UAVs is deployed to connect all ships with BS. This algorithm maintains the connectivity between UAVs and minimize the number of required UAVs at same time. The second sub-algorithm finds the optimal positions of UAVs and associations between UAVs, ships and BS for the lowest data transmission delay. A virtual force model is designed to adjust UAVs’ positions for lower transmission delay. Moreover, a network formation game model is developed to form a multi-hop network connecting ships to BS. Each ship and UAV selects the path connecting itself to BS for maximum utility. Simulation results shows that, the LDUD algorithm requires the minimum number of UAVs when the number of ships is more than 120. For the transmission delay from ships to BS, our algorithm improves more than 25% than other algorithms.

articleTitle: How to Design a R-D Model for UAV Video Transmission?
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) video transmission has been extensively applied in many crucial fields. However, the problem of designing a rate-distortion (R-D) model for UAV video transmission, which is essential for theoretical analysis of video coding and optimization of video transmission quality, is under-studied. The designed R-D model is desired to be simple, accurate, and generic owing to the limited capability of the UAV. Observing the key role of transformed residuals in the R-D model, this paper elaborately discusses the modeling of the transformed residual distribution and proposes an estimation algorithm to estimate the statistical parameter of the distribution. Specifically, considering the stringent requirements for low complexity and high generalization capability, we first design a linear parameter estimator by mining and analyzing UAV video statistical characteristics. Further, we develop a bias update scheme to improve the accuracy of the estimator. Test results on multiple real video sequences taken by UAVs show that the proposed estimation algorithm is more accurate than benchmarks.

articleTitle: Resource Allocation and 3D Trajectory Optimization for Relay Communication of UAV Swarm
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), valued for their compact size, light weight, and versatile deployment and recovery capabilities, have found extensive applications in both military and civilian domains. This paper introduces a joint optimization algorithm that incorporates user scheduling, UAV 3D trajectory, and transmission power (STP). To solve the non-convex nature of optimization problem, the optimization problem is decomposed into three sub-problems, namely, user scheduling, 3D flight trajectory, and transmission power, which could be solved separately by the Block Coordinate Descent (BCD) method. Additionally, for the 3D flight trajectory and transmission power sub-problems, equivalent formulations are introduced by employing relaxed variable reconstruction. Subsequently, the reconstructed sub-problems are iteratively solved using the Successive Convex Approximation (SCA) method. Simulation results validate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm in improving the minimum system throughput while ensuring fairness among device pairs.

articleTitle: Accurate Positioning with Single Vision Beacon: A Spatial Geometry Based Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: This paper proposes a visual positioning algorithm based on feature points and triangular structures on a quick response code (V-FTQ), which can achieve precise position and orientation estimation using only a monocular camera and a single quick response (QR) code beacon. In the considered system, a few QR codes are placed on the ceiling, and a user holds a camera in hand to capture one QR code for positioning. In particular, we first propose an efficient matching mechanism to match the feature points of the captured QR beacon to their projections in the image plane of the camera. Then, based on the geometry relations between the feature points and their projections, V-FTQ is able to calculate the coordinates of the feature points in the camera coordinate. Next, the pose and position of the user are estimated based on linear algebra and spatial geometry. Finally, a singular solution elimination scheme is further proposed to effectively eliminate incorrect solutions estimated by V-FTQ, remaining correct pose and position. The simulation results demonstrate that V-FTQ outperforms similar algorithms in terms of precision and robustness to noise.

articleTitle: A Class of Extended Generalized RDP Codes
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In 2022, [1] proposed a new construction for binary array codes with three parity columns, which can deduce some types of maximum distance separable (MDS) array codes. It was left as an open problem generalizing this construction to support more parity columns. This paper considers such a generalization and reveals it as a class of extended generalized RDP codes. We present the relationship between new codes and codes over all-one polynomial rings. Furthermore, we explicitly provide two new MDS array codes, one designed for four parity columns. We also propose two corresponding approaches for quickly computing syndromes of the new codes, both of which reach the lowest known asymptotic complexities.

articleTitle: Compressed Sensing and Kalman Filter Based Channel Tracking for mmWave Massive MIMO Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Millimeter wave (mmWave) communication system requires efficient yet accurate channel tracking to achieve high effective spectral efficiency. In this paper, we pay special attention to mmWave massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems and propose a channel tracking approach based on compressed sensing and Kalman filter. To be specific, the proposed approach first utilizes compressed sensing technique to estimate the angular parameters, which tackles the grid mismatch and angle crossing. Subsequently, the angle prediction, beam training, and angle update are jointly designed by exploiting the temporal channel correlation, including different levels of channel variations. Simulation results show that the proposed channel tracking has higher spectral efficiency and lower tracking error than traditional methods for mmWave massive MIMO systems.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Proximal Policy Optimization for Digital Twin-Assisted Computing Offloading in Internet of Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: To cope with high latency and communication overhead in the Internet of Vehicles (IoV), digital twin (DT) technology is employed in mobile edge computing (MEC) to provide real-time monitoring and analysis. In this paper, we investigate the DT-assisted IoV edge computing problem with the goal of minimizing the long-term task offloading cost in terms of the offloading latency, energy consumption, and cloud computing cost. Then, we propose a multi-objective reinforcement learning (RL)-based DT-assisted vehicular edge computing (VEC) solution, which utilizes a large amount of real-time mapping data from DT to train the neural network in RL. Through combining the multi-objective evolutionary algorithm based on decomposition (MOEA/D) and proximal policy optimization (PPO) algorithm, the agent can make task offloading decisions simultaneously under the unknown dynamics of the vehicular environment. Simulation results show the superiority of the proposed DT-assisted solution compared to other single-objective solutions and the counterparts without DT in terms of striking a long-term trade-off among multiple objectives.

articleTitle: Time-series Decomposition and Augmented Self-rescaling Graph Neural Network for Traffic Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: With the rapid development of urbanization, traffic forecasting has become a critical issue of intelligent transportation system (ITS). Recently, a large number of traffic forecasting methods have emerged and achieved good performance, but there are still many challenges in how to capture the spatial-temporal dependency, dynamicity and heterogeneity of traffic data. To address these problems, we propose a time-series decomposition and augmented self-rescaling graph neural network (TDASGNN) for traffic forecasting in this paper. Specifically, the proposed method first adopts the gate time-series decomposition with linear layer (GTDL) network to mine the temporal dependency via decomposing complex traffic data to trend series and seasonal series along time dimension. And then, the local augmented network (LANet) is also introduced to the TDASGNN for enhancing its expressive power via learning distribution of neighbor node representations conditioned on the central nodes representation. In addition, in order to capture more accurate spatial dependency and dynamicity from traffic data, the self-rescaling dynamic Jocabi graph neural network (SDJGNN) is introduced to the TDASGNN. Meanwhile, the self-rescaling mechanism of SDJGNN can avoid the scale distortion issue of graph neural network. Finally, the proposed TDASGNN is applied to traffic forecasting experiments on two public traffic datasets, including PEMS04 and METR-LA. The experimental results demonstrate that our proposed TDASGNN is superior to other state-of-the-art (SOTA) traffic forecasting methods.

articleTitle: Coding Principle and Information-Theoretic Limit of OAMP Receiver in Unitary-Transform Generalized Linear Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In wireless communications, the unitary-transform generalized linear system (GLS) has been widely used to evaluate the impact of nonlinear preprocessing on transceivers. Generalized approximate message passing (GAMP) is a state-of-the-art low-complexity signal recovery algorithm, but it is only applicable to independent and identically distributed (IID) Gaussian matrices. To overcome this limitation, generalized orthogonal AMP (GOAMP) has been developed for unitarily invariant matrices, however, its information-theoretic limit analysis is numerical and limited by the high-complexity linear minimum mean-squared error (LMMSE), which is difficult to be analyzed analytically. Meanwhile, it is unable to effectively utilize the properties of unitary matrices, rendering the information-theoretic analysis still complex. To address these issues, in this paper, we provide the achievable rate analysis and optimal coding principle for GOAMP in unitary-transform GLS with arbitrary input distributions, establishing its information-theoretic limit (i.e., maximum achievable rate). Specifically, the simplified variational state evaluation (VSE) of GOAMP are developed using the unitary matrix properties to analyze the achievable rate, and the optimal code principle is derived with goal of maximizing the achievable rate. In addition, it is rigorously proved that GOAMP outperforms GAMP in terms of asymptotic MSE with lower complexity. Furthermore, quantization is used as an example to demonstrate the maximum achievable rate and practical low-density parity-check (LDPC) code design for GOAMP. The optimized LDPC code can approach the threshold limit within 0.8 dB and overcome the decoding deterioration and even divergence of the existing state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: Channel Capacity Enhancement for Terahertz Massive MIMO Systems Relying on Line-of-Sight RIS
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: This paper investigates channel capacity in the reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS)-assisted multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems operating in the terahertz (THz) band. Specifically, we conceive an evolved version of RIS, namely line-of-sight (LOS)-RIS, where the RIS element spacing is increased to embrace the near-field effect. With the LOS-RIS, the channel capacity can be significantly enhanced even under LOS-only channels. First, we analyze the channel capacity associated with the LOS-RIS as the RIS element spacing increases under single-user scenario, elucidating the underlying reasons for the enlarged spacing. Then, the analysis is extended to multi-user scenario, which unleashes the potential of utilizing a single LOS-RIS to serve multiple users under LOS-only channels. Furthermore, to accommodate multiple users, we propose a passive beamforming scheme, where the large LOS-RIS is partitioned into multiple subarrays and the phase shifts of each subarray are tailored to steer the reflected beams towards the corresponding user. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed paradigm, which paves the way for supporting multi-user multi-stream THz communications under LOS-only channels.

articleTitle: Clothes Changing Person Re-identification Using Spatial Information and Clothes Sensitivity Awareness
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Person re-identification is a hot topic in the field of computer vision. In the long-term re-identification, due to the change of person clothes, person re-identification has become a difficult task. In view of the above difficulty, this paper proposes a dual-category recognition method for clothes-changing people, and use spatial attention mechanism to capture important information in the image. Then, the sensitivity awareness of clothes changes is further proposed to expand the clothes differences between categories and reduce the interference of similar clothes in clothes classification. This re-identification method based on clothes sensitivity awareness and spatial attention mechanism can realize the comprehensive extraction of clothes-independent features. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets have confirmed the effectiveness of the method.

articleTitle: Enhancing Monocular Depth Estimation Using Attention in Hybrid Network
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Within the realm of deep learning-based Monocular Depth Estimation (MDE), Vision Transformers (ViTs) have garnered substantial attention as a network framework owing to their unique structure and impressive attention mechanism. However, ViTs encounter limitations in effectively capturing spatial features and exhibit a lack of sensitivity towards local information when compared to Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). This study aims to address the underutilization of valuable local information by ViTs and the oversight of performance improvement facilitated by the decoder. To tackle these challenges, we propose a hybrid network that leverages the strengths of both ViTs and CNNs to enhance both local information and long-range dependencies. In the encoder stage, we introduce an innovative patch attention mechanism to capture varying levels of attention across diverse regions. Furthermore, in the decoder stage, a cross-attention mechanism is devised to enhance feature fusion. Through extensive experimentation on diverse datasets, including KITTI, DIW, DIODE, and Sintel, our approach achieves more effective and representative features, leading to significant performance improvements of up to 13.98% compared to the state-of-the-art benchmarks in the MDE task.

articleTitle: Diffusion-Generated Fake Face Detection by Exploring Wavelet Domain Forgery Clues
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Recently, diffusion models have shown remarkable success in generating high-quality images, making them potentially more difficult t o d etect t han G AN-generated i mages. In this paper, we address the emerging challenge of detecting face forgeries generated by diffusion models. We leverage insights from frequency artifacts in GAN-generated images and delve into the frequency domain characteristics of diffusion-generated images using both discrete Fourier transform (DFT) and Haar discrete wavelet transform (HDWT). Our investigation reveals that, while diffusion-generated images lack obvious DFT artifacts like those in GAN-generated images, they exhibit fewer high-frequency details compared to real images. Building upon these observations, our multi-scale network incorporates wavelet lifting and wavelet-spatial transformer blocks, enabling precise frequency decomposition and efficient f eature f usion. Experimental results on two generated datasets demonstrate the superior robustness of our proposed method compared to state-of-the-art forgery detection methods, making it an effective solution for identifying face forgeries produced by diffusion models. The dataset and code are open source at https://github.com/eecoder-dyf/Diffusion-Detection-WCSP2023.

articleTitle: Channel Model Mismatch Analysis for 3D Positioning in Massive-MIMO Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: The next-generation communication system will probably exploit the massive multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) technique and high carrier frequency, thus can provide large array aperture and large bandwidth to support the location-based services with high positioning accuracy. In massive MIMO systems, a plane array is usually utilized, thus we consider the three-dimensional (3D) positioning scenario. Due to the large array aperture and bandwidth, the user is probably located in a near-field (NF) region, thus it is no longer reasonable to use the common stationary narrowband far-field (FF) channel model in the 3D positioning scenarios. In this case, the true channel model may contain the model damages of spatial non-stationarity (SNS), beam squint effect (BSE) and spherical wave model (SWM). If the FF channel model instead of the true channel model is utilized in the positioning process, the problem of channel model mismatch occurs, and the positioning performance will be degraded. In this work, we evaluate the positioning error bound (PEB) of a true channel model by the Cramér-Rao bound (CRB), the PEB of a mismatched channel model by the misspecified CRB (MCRB), then investigate the performance loss by comparing the CRB and MCRB. Simulations show that in the NF region, the SWM has the largest impact on the model mismatch, and SNS has the smallest impact, while in the FF region, the impact of BSE is more significant.

articleTitle: Delay Sensitive Beam Hopping for Satellite Communication Systems Relying on Fully Decentralized Soft Actor-Critics
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: With the large-scale beam and diversity of resource in satellite communication, beam clustering and hopping are effective methods for mitigating conflicts between resource uti-lization and co-channel interference. However, conventional beam hopping methods ignore the importance of allocating resources in time and on demand to improve the user experience and resource utilization. To this end, we propose a delay sensitive beam hopping method for satellite communication systems. First, the beam-bandwidth resource allocation is decomposed into each cluster to efficiently manage large-scale beams. Then, the service failure rate (SFR) is defined to facilitate timely allocation, and the throughput is controlled by traffic demand to realize on-demand allocation. Furthermore, the fully decentralized Soft Actor-Critics (SACs) framework for the two-dimensional resource allocation is designed, where "N-coding" action mapping efficiently generates beam-bandwidth resource allocation schemes with a single agent. Simulation results indicate that the proposed method can always achieve a low SFR with a relatively high throughput for satellite communication.

articleTitle: Resource Allocation for Maximizing the Achievable Rate of THz Integrated Sensing and Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Terahertz (THz) communication and integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) are both foreseen to be the new trend for the 6G wireless communication. In this paper, a THz ISAC system of array-of-subarray structure is considered. It is assumed that time is divided into sensing and communication slots and the transmission power levels for the sensing and communication slots can be different. Then, an optimization problem to maximize the achievable communication rate with sensing constraint and peak power constraint is formulated. A threshold on the sensing range is identified, within which only the communication signal is enough for satisfying the sensing constraint. Subsequently, when the target is beyond the threshold, an algorithm to determine the optimal resource allocation policy is designed. Through numerical results, the theoretical characterizations, and the performance improvements of the proposed algorithm are justified.

articleTitle: Maximizing Energy Efficiency of HSRC: A Cache-Aided Time-Domain Power Allocation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: This paper presents a cache-aided time-domain power allocation (CaTDPA) for 5G high-speed railway communications (HSRC), where two kinds of users, online interactive application users (OIUs) and online non-interactive application users (ONIUs), are jointly taken into account. For OIUs, their minimum ground-train data rate demand is guaranteed. For ONIUs, their minimum cache-releasing data rate demand is guaranteed. To achieve the green HSRC design, an optimization problem is formulated to maximize the system energy efficiency (EE) by jointly optimizing the power allocation (PA) and cache releasing start time (CRST) subject to the constraints of total available energy, maximum transmit power, ONIUs’ ground-train data rate threshold, ONIUs’ cache-releasing data rate threshold, and causality of CRST. To address such a non-convex and fractional problem, a two-step solution is designed. First, with a given CRST, a Dinkelbach-based method is applied to obtain the correspondingly optimal PA. Second, the one-dimensional traversal method is used to find the optimal CRST. Experimental results show that our proposed CaTDPA achieves the maximum EE among multiple compared methods while meeting the requirements of OIUs and ONIUs. Moreover, EE will decrease as the OIUs’ ground-train data rate threshold and the train’s moving speed increase, while it is observed that the ONIUs’ cache-releasing data rate threshold has a relatively small effect on the EE of HSRC.

articleTitle: Deep Neural Network Based Matched-Field Geoacoustic Inversion
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Acoustic field inversion offers an efficient approach for estimating geoacoustic parameters and acquiring valuable geoacoustic characteristics. The matched-field inversion technique aligns the measured acoustic field with a copy acoustic field generated by an acoustic propagation model. By employing optimization algorithms in a high-dimensional parameter space, the technique searches for the best matching acoustic parameters, and Bayesian theory is then applied to further determine the parameter uncertainties. However, the traditional global optimization process and posterior probability density sampling in matched-field inversion require multiple calls of the acoustic propagation model, resulting in a considerable computational time cost. Although using a surrogate model can enhance time efficiency, it often compromises inversion accuracy. To address this challenge, we propose intergrating a deep learning-based pre-screening process into the conventional matched-field inversion. This innovative approach significantly reduces the number of calls, thereby reducing time costs without sacrificing accuracy. In this paper, we conduct experiments on matched-field inversion based on Deep Neural Networks with simulated data and measured data to validate its efficacy.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Holographic Surface-Aided Distributed Edge Computing
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: The recently advocated reconfigurable holographic surface (RHS) is anticipated to bring substantial improvement in communication throughput, especially for the multi-node scenarios. From this viewpoint, RHS is a natural fit to distributed edge computing, where the computation task is offloaded to multiple edge nodes for faster processing. Nonetheless, existing pioneering works on RHS mainly focus on its application in conventional wireless communications, and, to the best of our knowledge, its potential for elevating distributed edge computing performance remains unexplored. In this work, an RHS-aided distributed edge computing scheme is proposed, where the mobile device performs part of the task locally and exploits the RHS to distribute the rest to multiple edge nodes simultaneously. Considering both local computing latency and offloading latency, a latency minimization problem is formulated by jointly optimizing the task partitioning, the local computing frequency, the holographic beamforming of RHS, and the digital beamforming. To tackle this non-trivial non-convex problem, a joint communication and computation optimization algorithm is developed based on the generic block coordinate descent (BCD) framework. Particularly, the original problem is divided into three subproblems, and the task partitioning and local computing frequency, the holographic beamformer, and the digital beamformer are optimized efficiently and iteratively in each subproblem. In addition, simulations are conducted to validate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Decomposition-based Multi-Agent Distributional Reinforcement Learning for Task-Oriented UAV Collaboration with Noisy Rewards
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Collaborated unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are often deployed to perform complex tasks on the basis of multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL). However, the environmental disturbance, commonly leading to noisy observations (e.g., rewards, states), could significantly shape the performance of task-oriented UAV collaboration. Therefore, it becomes imperative to revolutionize the design of MARL, so as to capably ameliorate the annoying impact of noisy rewards. In this paper, we propose a novel decomposition-based multi-agent distributional RL method by approximating the globally shared noisy reward by a Gaussian mixture model and decomposing it into the combination of individual distributional local rewards, with which each agent can be updated locally through distributional RL. Besides, the optimality of the distributional decomposition is theoretically validated, while the design of loss functions is carefully calibrated to tackle the decomposition ambiguity. We also verify the effectiveness of the proposed method through extensive simulation experiments with noisy rewards.

articleTitle: Hybrid Beamforming Design for Multi-User and Multi-Target ISAC Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) has drawn increasing attention in 6G applications due to its ability of enabling hardware and energy sharing for simultaneous sensing and communication operations. In this paper, we investigate the hybrid beamforming (HBF) optimization for multi-user and multi-target ISAC systems aiming at maximizing the communication sum-rate while ensuring the radar requirement in transmit beampattern. We propose a two-step algorithm for the ISAC HBF optimization problem, where we first obtain the digital beamforming solution via fractional programming (FP) and majorization-minimization, and further optimize the hybrid precoder via a coordinate descent algorithm. Furthermore, we show that the proposed HBF design approach can be extended to the near-field scenario, as well as the two-step FP-based HBF optimization algorithm. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed PF-based HBF (FP-HBF) algorithm and demonstrate the performance trade-off between communication and sensing. Results also show that the proposed FP-HBF algorithm considering the near-field effect achieves significant performance improvement over the one without considering such effect.

articleTitle: Active IRS-Assisted Wireless Powered MEC Systems with Non-linear Energy Harvesting Model
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) is a promising solution to assist the wireless power transfer (WPT) and task offloading in wireless powered mobile edge computing (WP-MEC) systems. However, to alleviate the double-fading attenuation of IRS-involved links, passive IRS is conventionally equipped with a large number of reflecting elements (REs), resulting in large surface size. To solve this issue, we investigate an active IRS-assisted WP-MEC system, in which active IRS is deployed to amplify the incident signals instead of just adjusting phase shifts as passive IRS. The beamforming at multi-antenna hybrid access point (HAP) is utilized for further performance improvement. To capture the sensitive properties of energy harvesting (EH) circuits, a practically non-linear EH model is adopted. The tasks are assumed to be bit-wise independent, and thus the partial offloading policy is adopted to the wireless devices (WDs). Accordingly, we propose an efficient compute-while-offload mode, i.e., the offloaded tasks are executed as soon as they are received by the HAP, thereby making full use of the finite edge computing capability. We aim to maximize the sum computational rate (SCR) of all the WDs by jointly optimizing time allocation, beamforming designs of active IRS and HAP, as well as offloading strategies of WDs. An algorithm based on alternating optimization (AO) is proposed to tackle the non-convexity of this problem. Numerical results demonstrate the superiority of deploying active IRS over passive IRS.

articleTitle: Azimuth Deployment in Intelligent Reconfigurable Surface Aided MISO Communications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Intelligent reconfigurable surfaces (IRSs) can enhance the communication performance by smartly reconfiguring the wireless communication environment. In particular, the phase shifts can be configured to change the small-scale fading properties of the wireless channels, and the location and azimuth of the RIS panel can be optimally deployed to compensate the large-scale path loss. The former has been extensively studied in the literature while the azimuth deployment problem remains to be explored. In this paper, the azimuth deployment is studied for the downlink multiple-input single-output IRS-aided multi-user system. Our goal is to maximize the weighted sum rate (WSR) of users by jointly optimizing the active beamforming at the BS, the passive beamforming and the azimuth of the IRS, subject to the minimum rate constraint of each user and the total power constraint. An alternating optimization (AO) algorithm is proposed to obtain the optimal solutions. We also derive the closed-form expressions for the optimal solutions for the single user case, which provides tractable results and useful insights for the multiple user case in practice. Simulation results show that the WSR can be improved by 20.36% when IRS is deployed with the optimal azimuth. Moreover, it is necessary to focus the azimuth of the IRS to the users with higher QoS requirements.

articleTitle: Joint Precoding and Passive Beamforming for Sum-Rate Maximization in Multiple IRSs Assisted Downlink Cell-free Network under Statistical CSI
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In this work, multiple intelligent reflecting surfaces (IRSs) assisted cell-free communication network is proposed under statistical CSI. We aim to maximize sum-rate by optimizing transmit precoding and passive beamforming with discrete phase shifts jointly. In order to tackle the non-convex optimization problem, penalty dual decomposition (PDD) method based on weighted minimum mean-square (WMMSE) is involved in the procedure of optimization. First, WMMSE is applied to approximate the non-convex objective function into a tractable one. Then, many auxiliary variables are introduced for the purpose of utilizing PDD to decouple the variables. The effectiveness of the proposed algorithm in multiple IRSs assisted cell-free network can be demonstrated by simulation results.

articleTitle: An Efficient Learning Algorithm for Phase Shift Optimization in RIS-Aided MISO Wireless Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Due to dynamic change of the wireless environment, devising the local phase shift matrix for reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) can be a thought-provoking task. Therefore, in this paper, we come up with a deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based beamforming optimization algorithm for RIS-aided multiple-input single-output communication systems. To be precise, we exploit a DRL-based structure based on twin-delayed-deep-deterministic-policy-gradient (TD3) algorithm to automatically adjust the phase shift of each unit at RIS to maximize the downlink received signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). Simulation results show that the raised TD3 algorithm performs a higher received SNR than the conventional DRL algorithm with a reduced running time.

articleTitle: Energy Consumption Constrained Resource Cell Optimization Based on Multipoint Channel Charting
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: With the increasing demand for mobile users for high-speed data transmission services, the problem of energy consumption of mobile communication systems is becoming increasingly prominent. Resource cell coverage structure has been proposed to match the service distribution and improve energy efficiency (EE) of sixth generation (6G) mobile networks. Unlike traditional EE maximization under signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) or rate constraints, we maximize the system capacity under energy consumption constraints. Relying on the above coverage structure, this paper proposes a multipoint channel charting (MPCC)-based resource cell generation (RCG) method to improve system capacity under transmit power constraint. Specifically, we divide adjacent users on MPCC into the same resource cell to reduce the system interference and improve the capacity, by allocating orthogonal resource blocks (RBs) within the resource cell and multiplexing RBs between resource cells, respectively. Simulation results show that the proposed method provides significant gain in capacity while being resilient to inaccurate information on the wireless channels, without accessing location information from global navigation satellite systems (GNSSs).

articleTitle: Model-driven Learning for Cell-Free MIMO Beamforming with Compression Strategy
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Cell-free Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) system is an appealing solution to improve the performance of wireless communication systems. However, the system performance improvement is restricted by the capacity limitations of fronthaul links. To address this issue, a compress-and-forward scheme is introduced, and the joint optimization of precoding and fronthaul compression is considered. Existing algorithms for this joint optimization often involve high computational complexity and latency due to iterative processes, making them unsuitable for real-time implementation. In this paper, we propose a model-driven neural network-based deep learning method that leverages expert knowledge, i.e., the uplink-downlink duality, to characterize the structure of beamforming matrix using low-dimensional parameters. These parameters, referred to as "key features", are learned from the channel state information through a neural network. Simulation results show that the proposed method achieves performance close to the optimal solution while significantly reducing computational time.

articleTitle: Deep Compression Based Intelligent Power Allocation Algorithm for Internet of Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: The high-speed movement of vehicle brings about the rapid change of communication environment. This leads to a sharp increase in the exchange amount of vehicle environment status information (ESI), which results in the communication quality dissatisfaction for Internet of Vehicles (IoV) user. To achieve efficient resource allocation, how to reduce the ESI exchange imposes crucial challenge for the rate improvement of IoV. In this paper, we propose the ESI deep compression based intelligent power allocation (ECIA) algorithm for IoV. First, a deep neural network (DNN) is used to compress the complex ESI to reduce the amount of information exchange in IoV. Then, a decision network composed of the total power network and power allocation network is designed to maximize the sum rate of Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V) links. Finally, simulation results show that the proposed ECIA algorithm can effectively increase the sum rate of V2V links and guarantee the communication quality of IoV user.

articleTitle: Deadline-Aware Hybrid HARQ Scheme for Multi-devices Deterministic Transmission over 5G-TSN Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: This paper studies a deadline-aware hybrid retransmission scheme for an Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) system over the 5th generation and Time-Sensitive Networking (5G-TSN) system. In the considered model, multiple devices must transmit time-sensitive data flows to an edge server for real-time computing and industrial control.
