It achieves threshold perfect secrecy through the (k,n) threshold secret sharing (SS) scheme, and prevents unauthorized eavesdropping between users through source-joint coding. The secrecy and the efficiency optimality of the proposed scheme are proved.

articleTitle: A Novel Radio Frequency Fingerprint Extraction Method Against Variable Channel Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Radio Frequency Fingerprinting (RFF) technology has emerged as a powerful solution for access control in wireless networks. One of the main tasks in this process is removing channel interference to obtain reliable RFF features. This paper proposes a novel RFF extraction scheme based on channel reciprocity. When the uplink and downlink channels satisfy short-term reciprocity, this method calculates RFF features by estimating uplink and downlink Channel State Information (CSI) and dividing them. It can eliminate the multipath channel characteristics to the greatest extent, completely retain the hardware characteristics of the transceiver links, and is not affected by changing antennas. We also developed an RFF extraction and recognition system using ESP32 development boards. Experimental results show that the system can achieve a recognition rate above 96% in practical scenarios such as Non-Line-Of-Sight (NLOS).

articleTitle: Kuhn-Munkres Algorithm Based Hybrid Beamforming for Wideband Millimeter Wave MIMO Systems With Dynamic Subarrays
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Dynamic subarrays (DSs) is an energy-efficient and cost-effective hybrid beamforming structure for millimeter wave (mmWave) multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) communications. In this paper, we investigate the nonconvex hybrid beam-forming problem of maximizing the average spectral efficiency of the point-to-point wideband mmWave MIMO system with DSs, where the beam squints are also considered. To address the nonconvexity of this hybrid beamforming problem, we first exploit the singular value decomposition of each subcarrier channel and water-filling strategy to get the optimal fully-digital beamforming. We then propose to leverage the Kuhn-Munkres algorithm to get the hybrid beamforming from the obtained fully-digital solutions, aiming to guarantee that every radio-frequency chain is connected to at least one antenna. Besides, we analyze the computational complexity of the proposed design. Numerical results demonstrate the superiority of this work over the state of the art.

articleTitle: A Cluster-based User Authentication Protocol for Internet of Medical Things Deployment
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: User authentication has been recognized as a promising technique for secure communication in the Internet of Medical Things (IOMT). Considering the limited storage resources of sensor devices and the problem of user privilege segmentation under the serverless model, we investigate the establishment of secure associations between users and sensor clusters through fine-grained access control. Specifically, we utilize merkle clusters to perfectly realize hierarchical user permissions, replacing the original database permission verification. We propose a three-factor cluster-based user authentication protocol (3CUAP) in a serverless model, and utilize non-formal security analysis, Proverif tools, etc. to analyze the security performance and communication cost. Simulation results demonstrate the robustness of 3CUAP to cyber-attacks such as internal privilege escalation, and its applicability for IOMT devices with limited storage resources.

articleTitle: Embracing Uncertainty: A Diffusion Generative Model of Spectrum Efficiency in 5G Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Spectrum efficiency modeling is a crucial enabling technology for optimizing 5G networks. Neural networks have been employed to model the complex and nonlinear relationship between spectrum efficiency and other 5G network features, including reference signal received power (RSRP), modulation and coding scheme (MCS), and rank indicator (RI). However, the current neural network model can only produce deterministic predictions, disregarding the stochastic nature of wireless networks, which may lead to suboptimal network performance. To address this limitation and embrace the uncertainty, we propose a diffusion generative model that can learn the conditional distribution of spectrum efficiency given the information of RSRP, MCS, and RI, providing a more accurate representation of the inherent variability in wireless networks. Additionally, we introduce a novel neural network architecture that incorporates a U-Net structure with Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) as building blocks, facilitating efficient learning of the denoising function within the diffusion generative model. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed diffusion generative model accurately learns the statistical distribution of spectrum efficiency. Moreover, the proposed diffusion generative model yields improved fitting performance based on real-world measurements and enables quantification of uncertainty in spectrum efficiency modeling, which is essential for better network optimization.

articleTitle: Symbol Detection for Intelligent Reflecting Surface-aided Orthogonal Time Frequency Space Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) modulation is an emerging technique with potential advantages for next-generation communications in high-mobility scenarios. However, the received signals undergo a power decrease due to the non-coherent superposition of all symbols transmitted through wireless channels. To tackle this issue, we propose an intelligent reflecting surface (IRS)-aided OTFS system, which leverages the IRS to enable coherent combination of the received signals. Considering the IRS-aided single-input single-output (SISO)-OTFS systems, we first jointly design the OTFS symbol frame structure and IRS phase shifts to coherently strengthen the received signal power. Building upon the above system design, a low-complexity iterative interference cancellation (IIC) detector is proposed, and its detection performance is analyzed. Numerical results are presented to validate the effectiveness of the system design and the proposed IIC detector.

articleTitle: Adaptive Massive MIMO Hybrid Precoding Based on Meta Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) mmWave communication has emerged as a pivotal technology in the fifth generation (5G) mobile communication system, with hybrid precoding technology garnering significant attention. In this paper, a hybrid precoding scheme based on convolutional neural network (CNN) is proposed. By utilizing an analog precoder with a partial connection structure, the network size is reduced and convergence is facilitated. Compared to traditional algorithms, this approach reduces computational complexity and time overhead. However, similar to other deep learning algorithms, it lacks robustness as the trained network may not be adaptable to new environments. To address this limitation, this paper further proposes a hybrid precoding scheme based on meta-learning, enabling the CNN model to quickly adapt to changing environments.

articleTitle: Graph Optimization Based Localization Algorithm by Fusing VLP and VO
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Visible light positioning (VLP) has attracted considerable interest due to its high accuracy and low cost. However, VLP typically requires several light emitting diodes (LEDs) for positioning, which may lead to positioning failure in sparse LED layout or parts of the links are blocked. To address this challenge, we propose a novel graph optimization-based localization algorithm by fusing VLP and visual odometry (VO), termed GO-VLO. In the considered model, a few LEDs are deployed on the ceiling and broadcast positioning information, while a receiver equipped with a camera conducts GO-VLO to achieve precise positioning with limited LEDs. GO-VLO consists of a front end to process positioning information and a back end to further optimize the positioning results. In particular, VLP and VO are first used separately at the front end, thus obtaining two respective positioning results. Then, a visible-light visual odometry fusion mechanism is proposed to fuse the positioning results of VLP and VO preliminarily. To strengthen the constraints between frames and prevent location failure when VLP is unavailable, a novel graph optimization framework is further proposed in the back end, which notably takes the covisible feature points of two successive frames into consideration. Experimental results show that our proposed method attains a positioning accuracy of 4.93 cm in two dimension and 6.20 cm in three dimension under dense LED layout.

articleTitle: Dynamic Beam Hopping for LEO Satellites with Differentiated Traffic Demands
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In low earth orbit (LEO) satellite communication system, it is challenging to achieve on-demand service due to the differentiated traffic demands across both temporal and spatial dimensions. The beam hopping (BH) technology, which enables flexible scheduling of system resources based on the quantity of traffic demands, is regarded as a potential solution to this problem. However, in most cases, obtaining the actual amount of traffic demands is difficult, and instead, the traffic distribution statistics are available, which puts forward higher requirements for designing BH pattern. To address this issue, a state classification-based multi-satellite joint iterative BH (SCMJI-BH) pattern design algorithm is proposed. The proposed algorithm takes into account both temporal delay and the interference from both intra-satellite and inter-satellite beams. Then, a timedivision optimization framework is designed by estimating traffic volume and utilizing the distinction in traffic states among cells. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm can effectively guarantee service fairness and exhibit robustness for different traffic loads.

articleTitle: Contract-Matching Incentive Mechanism for UAV-Assisted Mobile Edge Computing
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In the unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) assisted edge computing networks, the UAVs act as mobile edge nodes to provide flexible communication and computation services to user equipment (UE). To enable efficient resource trading between the UAV and UE, it is of paramount importance to design an incentive mechanism that compensates for the costs of the UAVs, while preventing the UAVs from falsely reporting their private resource information. To address this issue, we propose a contract-matching integrated incentive mechanism in a multi-UAV and multi-UE network, where the UEs are unaware of the UAVs’ locations and computation frequencies. To deal with the asymmetric information, we employ contract theory to maximize each UE’s expected utility while encouraging the UAVs to truthfully participate in the edge computing service. Then, we adopt the Gale-Shapley algorithm to establish the one-to-one association between UAVs and UEs. Finally, simulation results validate that our proposed mechanism can achieve individual rationality, incentive compatibility, and improve UEs’ average utility compared with the benchmark algorithm.

articleTitle: A Lightweight Cache-Assisted Data Recovery Mechanism for Latency-Critical Data in IIoT
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Latency-critical applications in the industrial Inter-net of Things (IIoT) pose significant challenges to the networks in terms of transmission latency [1]. Especially when packet loss occurs, existing retransmission mechanisms that rely on end-to-end recovery involve long recovery latency, which significantly affects latency-critical applications. To reduce the long recovery latency, we propose a cache-assisted data recovery mechanism that can cache recently transmitted data at the intermediate nodes, e.g., switches and routers. More specifically, we set different timeout period values to different types of data to reduce the data loss detection latency and propose a lightweight replacement policy by considering data latency requirement, data size, and number of receivers to improve the caching efficiency. The simulation results show that the proposed approach has an up to 13 times improvement in terms of unsatisfied data ratio compared to traditional data recovery mechanisms without caching.

articleTitle: Open-Set Radio Frequency Fingerprint Identification via Uncertainty Awareness
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Radio frequency fingerprint (RFF) identification is a promising authentication paradigm in physical layer security (PLS). Despite the significant accuracy of deep learning (DL) based schemes, most of them follow the closed-set assumption. In real-world scenarios, a practical RFF identification framework needs to accurately classify known emitters and reliably reject unknown/abnormal classes. In other words, the model needs to be aware of the prediction uncertainty, i.e. know unknown. To this end, we propose an open-set RFF identification framework with the properties of uncertainty awareness. Specifically, we formulate open-set RFF identification from the evidential deep learning (EDL) perspective. By formalizing the distribution of the latent space with a normalizing flows model, we consider the estimated density as evidence and use it to parameterize a Dirichlet distribution based on the subjective logic theory. In this way, the model can be aware of the uncertainty of the current prediction, inferring whether the identified sample comes from known classes. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed scheme can achieve trustworthy uncertainty awareness in open-set scenarios.

articleTitle: Duration-adaptive Video Highlight Pre-caching for Vehicular Communication Network
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Video traffic in vehicular communication networks (VCNs) faces exponential growth. However, different segments of most videos reveal various attractiveness for viewers, and the pre-caching decision is greatly affected by the dynamic service duration that edge nodes can provide services for mobile vehicles driving along a road. In this paper, we propose an efficient video highlight pre-caching scheme in the vehicular communication network, adapting to the service duration. Specifically, a highlight entropy model is devised to balance the segments’ popularity and continuity between segments within a period of time, based on which, an optimization problem of video highlight pre-caching is formulated. As this problem is non-convex and lacks a closed-form expression of the objective function, we decouple multiple variables by deriving candidate highlight segmentations of videos through wavelet transform, which can quickly and accurately find chunks with peak popularity values. Then the problem is solved iteratively by a highlight-direction trimming algorithm, which is proven to be locally optimal. Simulation results based on a real-world video dataset demonstrate significant improvement in highlight entropy and jitter compared to benchmark schemes.

articleTitle: Full Quantum One-way Function Based on Quantum Hypergraph State
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Quantum one-way function (QOWF) was proposed for quantum cryptography, which was computable but almost irreversible in quantum polynomial time. Full quantum one-way function (F-QOWF) is one of the most important models of QOWF, which deals with quantum states. Although the universal construction of full quantum one-way function has been proposed, there is still little further discussion on the entangled input, specific function instantiation and application scenarios of F-QOWF. In this paper, we introduce quantum hypergraph states into the universal construction of F-QOWF. Quantum hypergraph states are highly entangled multi-party states constructed from the hypergraph. By applying quantum hypergraph states to the new F-QOWF, we generalize the universal construction of F-QOWF to entangled states. The application to quantum aggregate signature shows that quantum hypergraph states help the new F-QOWF be well applied to quantum multi-party cryptographic protocols.

articleTitle: A Novel Virtual Node-Based Multi-Controller Management Architecture for LEO Mega-Constellation Satellite Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: The development of 6G communication has made low earth orbit (LEO) satellite networks to be a critical component of global communication systems. The high density of LEO satellites enables mobile devices to have continuous communication. However, managing satellites in mega-constellation LEO satellite networks poses a scalability challenge due to the large number of LEO satellite nodes. Besides, due to the high mobility of LEO satellites, inter-satellite handover frequently occurs, which leads to the degradation of traffic QoS (Quality of Service). To address these issues, in this paper, we propose a novel virtual node-based multi-controller management architecture for LEO-satellite constellation networks, that can effectively shield the dynamics of satellite network topology. In specific, we first redefine the virtual node as a geographical area with clear boundaries. Then, we set up domain controllers in each virtual node to manage the satellites. Besides, we propose a handover algorithm to reduce delay jitter and delay by jointly considering the probability of handover and the cost of rerouting. We conduct simulations on Starlink Phase I and the results show that compared with benchmark algorithms, the proposed architecture can reduce the delay jitter by more than 50% and the delay by 10%.

articleTitle: The SINR Meta Distributions in Cellular-Connected UAV Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: In this work, we develop a systematic framework based on the tools from stochastic geometry to characterize the meta distributions of the downlink signal-tointerference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) of the typical aerial user (AU) in a cellular-connected unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) network. We utilize a practical channel model that accounts for both line-of-sight (LoS) and non-line-of-sight (NLoS) transmissions to characterize the air-to-ground (A2G) channel. Assuming that the A2G transmissions experience Nakagami-m small-scale fading channels, and the adoption of strongest average received signal strength (RSS)-based cell association scheme, we drive the exact analytical expressions for the conditional success probability (CSP) and its b<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> moment, which is then utilized to obtain the meta distribution. A moment matching approach is further adopted to approximate the meta distribution to a beta distribution, where the accuracy is validated by simulations. The analysis concludes that compared to the Rayleigh fading channel, more AUs have higher link reliability in the Nakagami-m fading channel. As the Nakagami-m parameter increases, the proportion of AUs with higher reliability also increases. Our framework can provide guidance for the setting of related parameters in the deployment strategy for cellular-connected UAV.

articleTitle: Trajectory Design for Multi-UAV-Assisted Data Collection: A Multi-agent Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are widely employed in wireless communication networks due to their remarkable flexibility and mobility. In this work, we study a multi-UAV-assisted data collection system, where multiple UAVs cooperatively harvest data from ground users (GUs). Aiming at minimizing the mission completion time, we first formulate the trajectory design problem as a min-max optimization problem, subject to the constraints of energy consumption and collision avoidance. Then, by applying the popular QMIX framework, we propose a multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (DRL) algorithm to optimize the trajectory of all UAVs. With the well-designed reward function, the proposed multi-agent DRL approach can coordinate all agents to achieve the final objective based on their local observations. Simulation results verify the superiority of the proposed multi-agent DRL approach over the benchmark algorithms in terms of the mission completion time.

articleTitle: A Low-Latency Routing Scheme with Traffic Balancing for LEO Satellite Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites play an important role in satellite networks owing to low-cost, low round-trip delay and high data rate. However, the rapid change of constellation topology makes routing an intractable problem. In a scenario where LEO satellite network serves communication between ground stations (GSs), we adopt virtual topology to shield the dynamics and develop an approach of unipath routing with aim to minimize the total latency of all packets. Inspired by queuing theory, we propose a new routing metric that jointly considers propagation, transmission and queuing latency, which is helpful for traffic distribution awareness and balancing. In addition, Routing Algorithm with Queuing Metric (RAQM) is proposed to calculate the route. Moreover, we have contributed to clarifying the routing latency of packets in detail and quantifying the ability of the constellation to support the traffic load. The simulation results show that the proposed scheme has advantages especially under the condition of heavy traffic load as it can effectively reduce queuing time and end-to-end latency. Furthermore, the proposed scheme can support up to 115% more traffic and avoid network congestion effectively when compared to the selected benchmarks.

articleTitle: Availability-Aware Group-Personalized Federated Learning in Wireless Edge Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Deploying federated learning (FL) algorithms in wireless edge networks presents significant challenges, including data heterogeneity at individual and group levels, and user availability. Current research primarily focuses on addressing individual-level data heterogeneity with various personalized FL (PFL) algorithms, while challenges persist in handling group-level heterogeneity and understanding the impact of user availability on the PFL process. To bridge this research gap, we propose an availability-aware group-personalized FL algorithm for generic wireless edge networks. Our algorithm effectively detects user availability during the learning process and addresses group-level data heterogeneity. Through rigorous analysis, we demonstrate its convergence performance under suitable conditions. Simulation results showcase the algorithm’s robustness in handling fluctuations in user availability and its effectiveness in addressing group-level data heterogeneity. Our work highlights the practical implications and potential applications of the proposed algorithm in real-world scenarios.

articleTitle: Secure Communication in RIS-assisted MIMO systems: Active RIS or Passive RIS?
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: As 6G technology continues to evolve, RIS is expected to play a significant role in addressing the challenges of future communication systems. Recently, to combat the "double fading" effect caused by the signal propagating over the reflected link in RIS-assisted systems, active RIS has been proposed and received significant attention. This paper focuses on addressing the issue of secure transmission at the physical layer in a multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) system aided by active RIS. In this system, the user (UE) receives multiple parallel streams of data sent from the base station (BS). Specifically, to enhance the anti-eavesdropping capability, we propose a formulation for maximizing the secrecy rate, which involves a non-convex problem. To solve this problem, we transform it into an equivalent form by exploiting the equivalence between the data rate and the minimum mean-square error (MMSE), and propose an efficient alternating optimization algorithm to optimize the BS precoder and RIS beamformer jointly. Simulation results validate that with the same power consumption, the secrecy rate is obviously improved in the active RIS assisted MIMO systems compared with the passive RIS case.

articleTitle: Design of an Active Detection and Supervision Mechanism for Malicious Interference cancellation in Vehicular Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: With the development of V2X communication technology, many issues, especially the security of information, are brought to light. Due to the multilateral participation and the unknown attributes between vehicles, V2X communication faces challenges in evaluating the credibility of road safety information. Moreover, the interference caused from malicious vehicles transmitting false information severely undermines the trust schemes’ decision-making process, ultimately leading to the occurrence of catastrophic accidents. To address these issues, we propose an active detection-based supervising mechanism’s hybrid trust model in which vehicles record the credibility of surrounding vehicles nodes through active detection. Vehicles can report their detection records to the RSU, which updates the trust scores of vehicles by fusing three reference factors using analytic hierarchy process (AHP) hierarchy analysis. Simulation experiments demonstrate that our proposed model not only enhances the suppression of malicious vehicles, but also penalizes malicious supervisor.

articleTitle: IRS-Enabled Physical Layer Secure Transmission
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Due to the broadcast nature of multi-hop channels, the information security of intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) assisted wireless communication remains an open issue to be resolved, which is even more urgently in the case that the passive eavesdropper is directly linked with the transmitter of a single-input single-output (SISO) transmission system. To deal with this, in this paper, we propose a transmitter perturbation injection and IRS reflection based physical-layer security scheme, such that the secure transmission of wireless SISO can be guaranteed comprehensively no matter the reflection based jamming from IRS to the eavesdropper is blocked or not. Upon considering this, two different eavesdropping scenarios, which are referred to as the ideal and worst eavesdropping, are considered and investigated. In addition, we propose element-wise and group-wise phase-alignment based reflection strategies respectively, so as to attain different trade-offs between the achievable performance and implementation complexity. In order to evaluate the achievable performance limits, we analyze the ergodic secrecy rate (ESR) of the proposed system. Simulation and numerical results verify the accuracy of performance evaluations. Finally, the effectiveness of our proposed secure transmission scheme is demonstrated by comparing the ESR performance achievable by it with that by the random-phase reflection based counterpart.

articleTitle: Meta-Reinforcement Learning for UAV-Assisted Mobile Edge Computing of Virtual Reality Services
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Virtual reality (VR) services face significant challenges, such as large-volume data transmission, high computing demands, and extreme latency sensitivity, particularly on wireless VR devices with limited resources. Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-assisted mobile edge computing (MEC) emerges as a promising solution to ease the computational burden on user devices and enable efficient VR service delivery. This paper proposes a UAV-assisted collaborative MEC framework, involving one access point (AP), one UAV, and VR users, catering to various VR scenarios. VR videos are cached in 2D field of view (FoV) format at the AP, while users request 3D FoV rendering. The 3D FoV model is derived via edge computing at the AP, UAV, or VR users. We formulate an optimization problem with the objective of maximizing VR users’ average service completion rate (ASCR) while minimizing UAV energy consumption, subject to UAV movement, energy, and transmit power constraints. Then, we model the problem as a Markov decision process (MDP) and employ meta-reinforcement learning (Meta-RL) for an optimal strategy. Extensive simulations confirm the efficacy of our approach in enhancing the user experience, efficiently leveraging UAV capacities for edge computing and communications. The robust generalization ability of our Meta-RL algorithm ensures suitability for diverse real-world scenarios.

articleTitle: Space-Frequency Modulation based Waveform Design for Radar-Communication Integrated System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)
abstract: Space-frequency modulation (SFM) technology enables the mapping of one-dimensional communication data onto both spatial and frequency dimensions, making it suitable for the co-design of integrated radar and communication waveforms. In this paper, we propose an SFM-based integrated waveform, which significantly improves the communication rate and peak side-lobe ratio performance compared to the existing design. To recover the embedded communication data in the proposed waveform, we introduce a maximum likelihood (ML) demodulation scheme as well as a low-complexity suboptimal demodulation scheme. Finally, we numerically evaluate the performances of the proposed waveform and demodulation schemes, comparing with the state-of-the-art algorithms. Simulation results demonstrate that communication rate can be increased by 30% given the selected frequencies as 24 and the number of sub-pulse as 5.
